title: Converging quality by design, artificial intelligence, and biofoundry automation: A new paradigm for scalable circular biomanufacturing.
text: Synthetic biology applies engineering principles to the rational design of biological systems with the aim of producing predictable and tunable behaviour. Although the field's conceptual foundations and core technologies are well established, the recent simultaneous maturation of Quality by Design (QbD), artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted biological design, and automated biofoundry workflows is beginning to outline a more replicable pathway from laboratory innovation to industrial-scale circular biomanufacturing. This review argues that the convergence of these three elements, rather than any one alone, characterises the current phase of the field. We examine how the Design-Build-Test-Learn (DBTL) cycle is being transformed from a research heuristic into a systematic industrial development framework; show how shared toolsets now transfer across microbial, plant, and animal systems to enable a holistic bioeconomy; benchmark synthetic biology-derived products against conventional alternatives where techno-economic and life-cycle data permit; and examine scale-up, regulatory, and societal bottlenecks through recent market-scale case studies in which these bottlenecks have been navigated in practice. We also contrast EU and US regulatory frameworks to show how policy divergence shapes technology adoption. We conclude by identifying what the coming decade of convergent synthetic biology must deliver to support a circular bioeconomy at the scale the 2030 Agenda demands.

title: Artificial intelligence for vascular minimally invasive surgery: techniques, clinical integration, and challenges.
text: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including endovascular and robot-assisted procedures, is widely used for vascular pathologies but remains limited by technical complexity, cognitive workload, and postoperative complications. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may help address these challenges through predictive analysis, decision support, image analysis, and automation. A structured Google Scholar search was conducted from February 21, 2025, to January 1, 2026, and updated through September 2026. Peer-reviewed studies applying AI to vascular MIS were included, with additional targeted searches addressing clinical translation, deployment, regulation, and ethical considerations. Thirty primary studies were analyzed, including eight on machine learning, nine on deep learning, four on natural language processing, and nine on robotics or reinforcement learning. Machine learning supported risk stratification and outcome prediction, deep learning enabled imaging and segmentation applications, natural language processing facilitated clinical information extraction, and robotic systems supported navigation and procedural assistance. AI demonstrates substantial potential across the vascular MIS pathway, but broader clinical adoption requires stronger validation, prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, health-economic evaluation, and careful consideration of regulatory, liability, and accessibility challenges.

title: Longevitomics as the Science of the Longevitome: Towards a Unified Systems Science of Healthy Longevity.
text: The twenty-first century has transformed longevity research through genomics, epigenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, microbiome science, digital phenotyping and artificial intelligence. Yet healthy longevity remains difficult to explain because its determinants are commonly studied as separate molecular layers, mechanisms or biomarkers. Here, we introduce Longevitomics as an integrative systems framework for understanding, modeling and predicting healthy longevity and define the Longevitome inspired by the Latin expression vita longa (long life) as the dynamic architecture of biological, environmental and behavioral determinants that collectively shape psychosomatic resilience across the life course. We position this proposal in relation to the Hallmarks of Aging, geroscience, biological-age biomarkers, multi-omics and systems medicine. Longevitomics is not intended to replace these established frameworks or to constitute another molecular "ome." Rather, it provides a systems-level framework in which mechanistic hallmarks, multi-omic layers, physiological phenotypes, exposures and adaptive responses can be integrated longitudinally. We further consider how network analysis, causal inference, machine learning and digital-twin approaches may enable reconstruction of individual Longevitome trajectories and support a transition toward predictive and personalized longevity medicine.

title: The road ahead for stem cell therapies in type 1 diabetes.
text: Type 1 diabetes results from autoimmune destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells. Although exogenous insulin remains the standard treatment, it does not restore physiological glucose regulation. Differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells into β-cells offers a scalable alternative to cadaveric islet transplantation and has progressed rapidly over the past decade, resulting in nine clinical trials at various stages of completion. Despite this progress, durable graft function remains constrained by two major challenges: the absence of key islet microenvironment components, such as vasculature, extracellular matrix and supporting cell types and continued vulnerability to autoimmune and alloimmune rejection. This review considers emerging technological approaches to overcome these barriers. Bioengineered niches, including multilineage organoids, functionalized hydrogels, decellularized matrices and bioprinting, aim to recreate the native islet microenvironment, while synthetic biology approaches, such as hypoimmune gene editing, CRISPR-based transcriptional control and stimulus-responsive survival circuits, seek to enhance grafts' resilience. Computational and single-cell approaches, including gene regulatory network analysis and digital twin frameworks, are beginning to provide predictive tools for benchmarking differentiation quality and forecasting graft outcomes. Together, these complementary strategies, potentially tailored to individual patients, represent a realistic path towards safer, more effective and durable β-cell replacement therapies for type 1 diabetes.

title: Theranostic Imaging Agents: Integrating Molecular Diagnostics, Precision Therapeutics, and Artificial Intelligence.
text: Theranostic imaging agents combine molecular diagnosis, targeted therapy and monitoring of treatment response into a single paradigm of precision medicine. This review summarizes the current development and translational landscape of theranostic imaging agents, covering molecular targets, imaging platforms, principles of agent design, nanotheranostics, radiotheranostics, and disease-specific applications. Particular emphasis is given to clinically validated and emerging targeting strategies using prostate-specific membrane antigen, somatostatin receptors, fibroblast activation protein, C-X-C Chemokine Receptor 4 (CXCR4), Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (HER2) and other disease-associated biomarkers. Moreover, the review addresses Positron Emission Tomography (PET), Single-Photon Emission Computed Tomography (SPECT), Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), optical, photoacoustic, Raman and multimodal imaging approaches, therapeutic payloads, stimulus-responsive systems, and pharmacokinetic optimization. Moreover, emerging applications of artificial intelligence, radiomics, radiogenomics, spatial and single-cell multiomics, liquid biopsy, digital pathology, personalized dosimetry, and digital twins are evaluated for their potential to improve patient stratification, treatment selection, response assessment and adaptive therapy. Despite tremendous progress, clinical translation is hampered by target heterogeneity, off-target accumulation, radionuclide availability, manufacturing complexity, dosimetric uncertainty, regulatory requirements, limited clinical validation, data interoperability, cost and unequal access. This review, overall, emphasizes the convergence of molecular imaging, targeted therapeutics, nanotechnology, and artificial intelligence in the development of next-generation theranostic platforms, and outlines critical priorities for their clinical translation.

title: Digital twin technology in cardiovascular care: future perspectives for nursing practice, patient management, and clinical decision-making.
text: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality globally and continue to impose substantial clinical, economic, and organisational burdens on healthcare systems due to increasing disease complexity, recurrent hospitalisations, and the need for long-term monitoring and personalised care. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence, computational modelling, wearable biosensors, telehealth, and digital health technologies have accelerated the emergence of Digital Twin Technology (DTT) as a promising innovation in precision cardiovascular healthcare. Although DTT has gained growing attention in medicine and engineering, its implications for cardiovascular nursing practice, patient management, and clinical decision-making remain insufficiently synthesised. This scoping review aimed to explore the current applications of DTT in cardiovascular healthcare and examine its implications for cardiovascular nursing practice, patient management, clinical decision-making, and future healthcare delivery. Review was conducted using the Arksey and O'Malley methodological framework and reported according to the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar was performed for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Eligible studies included literature related to digital twins, computational cardiovascular modelling, artificial intelligence-assisted cardiovascular care, wearable technologies, remote monitoring systems, and nursing implications in cardiovascular healthcare. Data were charted and synthesised narratively according to predefined research questions and thematic areas. Thirty studies met the inclusion criteria. The findings demonstrated that DTT is increasingly applied in heart failure monitoring, arrhythmia prediction, telecardiology, smart ICU systems, virtual cardiac modelling, personalised rehabilitation, and population-level cardiovascular risk prediction. Artificial intelligence, machine learning, wearable biosensors, cloud computing, electronic health records, and predictive analytics were the most commonly reported technological components. The review further identified important implications for cardiovascular nursing, including transition from reactive to predictive care, expansion of telehealth nursing, enhanced data-driven clinical decision-making, and the growing need for digital competency. However, ethical concerns, cybersecurity risks, interoperability challenges,infrastructure costs, workforce preparedness, and limited nursing-focused evidence remain significant barriers. DTT has the potential to transform cardiovascular healthcare through predictive, personalised, and continuously adaptive models of care. Strengthening nursing leadership, digital competency and interdisciplinary collaboration is essential for integration of DTT into future cardiovascular practice.

title: A Non-interventional, International, Multicentre Clinical Research Study to Build the Largest Collection of Multimodal Data (Including Clinical Data, Imaging Data and Omics Data) in Oncology
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING] Cancer is amongst the leading causes of disease-related morbidity and mortality. A major challenge in cancer treatment is the development of biology-informed, personalised treatment strategies. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies have shed further insights into disease biology and treatment pathways, thus identifying new, precision medicine-based therapeutic opportunities. The biological mechanisms leading to cancer development and progression arise from complex and plastic networks of dysregulated cellular programs involving many signalling pathways and effector molecules. Cancer cells alter their surrounding environment via cell-cell interactions with non-tumor cells or by secreting cytokines, chemokines and other factors. This reprogramming of the tumour microenvironment (TME) is critical for cancer progression, invasion, and metastasis. Moreover, there are increasing studies that show that both innate and adaptive immune cell types contribute to tumorigenesis and treatment resistance when present within the TME. Understanding the crosstalk between cancer cells and the surrounding TME will inform on mechanisms of sensitivity and resistance to treatment, including immunotherapy (IO) and targeted therapies. Spatially resolved-Omics is an emerging field that characterises cell types by gene/protein expressions within their spatial context in the tissue organisation. Recent high profile spatial transcriptomics studies have uncovered specific cell identities that define the surrounding TME. The MOSAIC study, a collaborative initiative across industry and top oncology hospitals, proposes to go way beyond current cancer molecular profiling projects by combining the generation and analysis of multiple data modalities (3 essential mandatory modalities: Clinical Data, Hematoxylin and Eosin (H\&E) microscopic image, Spatial transcriptomics; up to 3 high priority data modalities depending on technical feasibility and sample size: bulk Ribonucleic Acid Sequencing (RNAseq), bulk Whole Exome Sequencing (WES), Single-cell transcriptomics; and potentially other optional data modalities and follow-up experiments such as single-cell omics, immunohistochemistry and spatial proteomics or other molecular profiling of proteins and molecules) on a minimum of 2,000 tumour samples across a different cancer indications. This will generate broad molecular and cellular profiling data of the tumour and its microenvironment from cancer patients, integrated with clinical data, at an unprecedented scale and resolution. This study will enroll patients diagnosed with one of the eligible cancer indications and for which a formalin fixed paraffin embedded (FFPE) tumor sample from already performed biopsy and/or surgical resection is available within their local pathology archive or their affiliate centers archives. The MOSAIC study expects to have a strong impact for patients in terms of new targeted therapeutic drug discovery, identification of patient subgroups requiring either specific treatment or broader clinical care and identification of novel treatment response and resistance mechanisms.

title: GenoMed4ALL: Improving SCD Classification and Prognosis by AI
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: UNKNOWN] GenoMed4All 'Genomics and Personalized Medicine for all though Artificial Intelligence in Haematological Diseases' aims to advance on individual SCD patients' disease characterisation and to improve the monitoring of patients' health status, optimise clinical therapy guidance and ultimately improved health outcomes by the identification of biomarkers and the development of individual (risk) models in SCD. Genomed4All supports the pooling of genomic, clinical data and other "-omics" health through a secure and privacy respectful data sharing platform based on the novel Federated Learning scheme, to advance research in personalised medicine in haematological diseases thanks to advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) models and standardised interoperable sharing of cross-border data, without needing to directly share any sensitive clinical patients' data. The SCD Use case will gather multi-modal clinical and -OMICs data from 1,000 SCD patients in 4 EU-MS: France, Italy, Spain and The Netherlands. In close collaboration with the European Reference Network on Rare Hematological Diseases (ERN-EuroBloodNet, GA101157011), GENOMED4ALL involves multiple clinical partners from the network, while leveraging on healthcare information and repositories that will be gathered incorporating interoperability standards as promoted by ERN-EuroBloodNet central registry, the European Rare Blood Disorders Platform.

title: Gene Therapy: Advances in Delivery Systems, Genome Editing Technologies, and Applications in Human and Veterinary Medicine.
text: Gene therapy has emerged as a revolutionary therapeutic strategy for the treatment of inherited, acquired, and age-related diseases through the modification, replacement, or correction of defective genes. Advances in molecular biology, viral engineering, and genome-editing technologies have significantly enhanced the efficiency and safety of gene delivery systems. This review provides a comprehensive overview of gene therapy, including its classification, delivery methods, and therapeutic applications in both human and veterinary medicine. Viral vectors such as adenoviral, retroviral, lentiviral, adeno-associated viral, and poxviral vectors remain the most effective delivery platforms owing to their high transduction efficiency, whereas non-viral approaches including physical and chemical delivery systems offer improved biosafety and reduced immunogenicity. Recent developments in gene-editing technologies, particularly clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-associated protein systems, have expanded the therapeutic potential of gene therapy by enabling precise genome modifications. The review highlights the successful application of gene therapy in treating genetic disorders, cancer gene therapy, retinal diseases, neuromuscular disorders, hemophilia, and metabolic diseases in humans, as well as inherited and acquired diseases in companion and livestock animals. Despite remarkable progress, challenges related to delivery efficiency, immune responses, off-target effects, manufacturing scalability, regulatory approval, and long-term safety continue to limit widespread clinical implementation. Advances in vector design, genome-editing precision, artificial intelligence-assisted development, and regulatory frameworks are expected to address these limitations. Overall, gene therapy and CRISPRbased technologies represent promising platforms for the development of next-generation precision medicines that could transform disease management in both human and veterinary healthcare.

title: Artificial intelligence apps for medical image analysis using pyCERR and cancer genomics cloud.
text: To provide a software resource that enables medical researchers and practitioners to develop and apply reproducible, out-of-the-box, AI-based analysis workflows for radiological and radiotherapy data. The framework comprises two main components: the Python-native computational environment for radiological research (pyCERR) for radiological image processing, and the cancer genomics cloud (CGC), a National Cancer Institute-funded resource that supports cloud-hosted collaborative projects, with tools for managing collaborators and compute-hardware from providers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud Platform. pyCERR is open-source (GNU GPL) and distributed at https://github.com/cerr/pycerr; it provides user-friendly data structures, simplified access to metadata across radiological imaging modalities, and tools for data transformation, AI-based image segmentation, radiomics, dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI analysis, radiotherapy dose-volume histogram (DVH) feature extraction, and normal-tissue complication and tumor-control models. Radiomics features comply with the Image biomarker standardization initiative (IBSI) standards and are validated against published reference values. Unit tests covering data input/output, radiomics, DVH features, and visualization run on every code update. Workflows are containerized for reproducible, identical execution on the CGC and on local hardware. The CGC enables AI inference from radiological images to be combined with other data types such as genomics and proteomics. Our public CGC project (https://cgc.sbgenomics.com/u/sevenbridges/pycerr-radiological-radiotherapy-imageanalysis), accessible with free registration, currently includes apps for organ-at-risk (OAR) and lung-nodule segmentation based on published models trained in-house and clinically validated. These apps can be run interactively from a web browser or programmatically via a REST API with client support for multiple programming languages. Notebooks demonstrating the CGC API and pyCERR capabilities are provided at https://github.com/cerr/pycerr-notebooks. The framework facilitates end-to-end radiological image analysis and reproducible research, including data access from public and private repositories, training and inference with AI models, and utilities for data management, visualization, and simplified access to image metadata.

title: Building Capacity for the Engineering of Biology and Biomanufacturing in Finland.
text: Finland's efforts on engineering biology (synthetic biology) originate from the investments in genetic engineering at the beginning of 1980s. The efforts were linked early on with industry, such as dairy companies, vaccine production and production of ethanol and industrial enzymes, and development of commercial scale bioprocesses. Timely support for activities in metabolic engineering, systems biology and genome wide technologies (omics) and incorporating bioinformatics and cell level modelling evolved the field naturally towards synthetic biology and biofoundry activities. This foundation has created a strong basis in industrial biotechnology in particular, its insights and capabilities being increasingly relevant today within the green transition and bioeconomy contexts. In Finland, more than 830 companies are categorised to operate in biotechnology, collectively producing a turnover of 7.1 billion euros and providing jobs for around 19,400 people. Technology and business opportunities are developing fastest in the field of modern biotechnology rooted in molecular biology. Consequently, in the past 15 years, Finland has evidenced the founding of many new biotechnology firms. In relation to bioeconomy, Finland has also a significant research tradition in plant biotechnology and breeding and in pilot scale cultivation of plant cells. Furthermore, engineering biology activities within medical biotechnology and diagnostics are strong. According to a recent report, 88.5% of the revenue of Finnish biotechnology companies comes from activities classified as industrial biotechnology. This article focuses on engineering/synthetic biology developments for industrial biotechnology, including microbial production of food components and pharma products.

title: From Static Records to Virtual Digital Patients: An Artificial Intelligence-Driven Framework for Medical Data Assetization and Governance.
text: Healthcare data remain difficult to use because of fragmentation, sensitivity, and overlapping rights and responsibilities. A virtual digital patient links a longitudinal representation of an individual patient with modeling capabilities for specified clinical or research questions. This article proposes a conceptual socio-technical framework for governing how virtual digital patients are created, accessed, used, and updated. A narrative synthesis of selected policy, modeling, interoperability, and health artificial intelligence literature informs four interdependent layers: data and representation; artificial intelligence modeling and simulation; governance and control; and clinical and external use. The framework connects standardized longitudinal representations, knowledge-supported reasoning, disease-specific simulation, authorization, output review, lifecycle management, and accountability. It distinguishes data resources, model services, operational capabilities, and potentially recognizable assets; technical functionality alone does not establish asset status. An illustrative oncology trial-design scenario shows how purpose-limited requests could produce bounded, reviewed outputs without transferring raw patient records. A staged validation agenda addresses data quality, model performance, workflow safety, clinical utility, and governance controls. The article reports neither a new algorithm nor a deployed or clinically validated system. Its contribution is an integrated reference architecture for evaluating how patient-specific modeling, institutional stewardship, and value return may be aligned. Disease-specific implementation and empirical evaluation are required before clinical or commercial claims can be established.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven precision management of Helicobacter pylori: an integrated framework from endoscopy and multi-omics to vaccine design and digital care.
text: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection, affecting half of the world's population, is the principal cause of peptic ulcer disease and gastric cancer, yet its clinical management is increasingly undermined by the rapidly escalating global burden of antibiotic resistance, the suboptimal accuracy of conventional diagnostic methods, and the declining efficacy of empirical therapeutic regimens. Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping this landscape, but existing research remains fragmented across single modalities. We propose a conceptual five-module framework that integrates AI approaches across the H. pylori care continuum: (1) global disease burden and the evolutionary dynamics of H. pylori drug resistance; (2) the application of multimodal AI, from convolutional neural networks to vision-language foundation models, for endoscopic early screening, pathological identification, and functional assessment; (3) the harnessing of machine learning (ML) on genomic and electronic health record data to decipher resistance mechanisms and generate personalized eradication regimens; (4) AI-driven vaccine target discovery and generative design, spanning reverse vaccinology to de novo immunogen creation; and (5) a digital closed-loop patient management platform that leverages new media and reinforcement learning to enhance adherence and eradication rates. We further delineate the core challenges of data bias, cross-scenario generalization, and the critical absence of prospective randomized evidence, and propose a future direction anchored in multimodal foundation models, federated learning, and continuous AI quality improvement. Rather than an established clinical pathway, this framework is proposed as a conceptual blueprint that, once prospectively validated, could upgrade AI-enabled H. pylori care from isolated image recognition toward an end-to-end "perception-reasoning-intervention" system, offering a blueprint for precision prevention and control.

title: Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression
text: Abstract Understanding the genetic basis of gene expression can shed light on the regulatory mechanisms underlying complex traits and diseases. Single cell-resolved measures of RNA levels and single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTLs) have revealed genetic regulation that drives sub-tissue cell states and types across diverse human tissues. Here, we describe the first phase of TenK10K, the largest-to-date dataset of matched whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq). We leverage scRNA-seq data from over 5 million cells across 28 immune cell types, and matched WGS, from 1,925 individuals, which provides power to detect associations between rare and low-frequency genetic variants that have largely been uncharacterised in their impact on cell-specific gene expression. We map the effects of both common and rare variants in a cell type-specific manner using a recently introduced method that increases power by modelling single cells directly rather than relying on aggregated ‘pseudobulk’ counts. We identify putative common regulatory variants for 83% of all 21,404 genes tested and cumulative rare variant signals for 47% of genes. We explore how genetic effects vary across cell type and state spectra, develop a framework to determine the degree to which sc-eQTLs are cell type-specific, and show that about half of the effects are observed only in one or a few cell types. By integrating our results with functional annotations and disease information, we also further characterise the likely molecular modes of action for many disease-variant associations. Finally, we explore the effects that genetic variants have on gene expression across continuous cell states and functions, and effects that vary cell state abundance directly.

title: Current applications of artificial intelligence for advancing agriculture, sustainability and climate mitigation
text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping agriculture by enabling data-driven decision-making across crop production systems and supporting the transition toward more sustainable, resilient, and climate-smart farming. This review critically synthesizes advances in AI applications spanning precision irrigation, nutrient and soil management, yield prediction, pest and disease monitoring, computer vision, autonomous agricultural robotics, and large language model (LLM)-based decision support systems. Beyond summarizing technological developments, the review evaluates their practical deployment, emphasizing that successful agricultural AI depends not only on predictive accuracy but also on model generalizability, explainability, economic feasibility, interoperability, and integration with existing agronomic knowledge. Emerging technologies including Vision Transformers, foundation models, Digital Twins, multimodal AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and federated and continual learning—are discussed as important directions for overcoming limitations related to data scarcity, environmental variability, and scalable field implementation. The review highlights that responsible AI adoption requires transparent governance frameworks addressing data ownership, privacy, algorithmic fairness, cybersecurity, and equitable access, particularly for smallholder farming systems. Although numerous AI models report outstanding performance, widespread agricultural adoption remains constrained by cross-region validation, fragmented datasets, infrastructure requirements, and insufficient real-world deployment. Future progress will depend on multidisciplinary collaboration integrating advances in artificial intelligence, sensing technologies, robotics, crop science, and agricultural engineering to develop robust, trustworthy, and farmer-centered decision-support systems. By critically evaluating technological innovations and implementation challenges, this review provides a framework for understanding the current state of AI in agriculture while identifying research priorities that will shape the next generation of sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural systems.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Telemedicine: Transforming Diagnosis and Personalized Care in Virtual Health Systems
text: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) within telemedicine has revolutionized virtual healthcare delivery by enabling high-precision diagnostics and tailored treatment strategies remotely. This paper evaluates state-of-the-art AI models applied to medical imaging and clinical text data within telehealth platforms, highlighting significant improvements in diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision support. Using deep learning architectures like ResNet-50 for imaging and BERT for natural language processing of electronic health records, the framework demonstrates enhanced patient care personalization and operational efficiency. Survey feedback from clinicians and patients underscores AI's practical benefits in improving healthcare accessibility and quality in remote settings. Challenges, including algorithmic biases and data privacy risks, are discussed, along with future research directions aimed at sustaining AI-driven telemedicine enhancements to health systems worldwide.

title: Yeast-Based Platforms for Next-Generation Human Health Applications
text: Yeast platforms are rapidly transitioning from traditional eukaryotic model organisms to versatile, programmable chassis for next-generation human health applications. This review systematically examines the translational evolution of conventional and non-conventional yeasts including Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Komagataella phaffii, Saccharomyces boulardii, and Yarrowia lipolytica and redefines them as scalable biomanufacturing factories and advanced living therapeutics. We highlight milestone advancements in synthetic biology toolkits that lower technical barriers, such as CRISPR-mediated multiplex editing, modular cloning frameworks, and high-throughput secretion screening. We focus on sophisticated glycoengineering strategies for humanized N-glycosylation, alongside data-driven paradigms that leverage artificial intelligence to predict gene expression and streamline strain design. In clinical domains, we detail the established success of yeast in producing subunit or virus-like particle vaccines (e.g. HBV and HPV) and therapeutic enzymes (e.g. ecallantide), alongside its emerging role as gut-adapted live biotherapeutic products (LBPs) engineered for in situ delivery and biosensing. Finally, we explore specialized non-conventional platforms, focusing on lipid- and acetyl-CoA-rich hosts for lipophilic drug discovery, and stress-tolerant systems optimized for economical, feedstock-flexible bioprocesses. In summary, this review underscores the integrated value of yeast systems across disease modeling, industrial manufacturing, and clinical intervention, charting future directions to address global health challenges.

title: Registry of an Integrated Longitudinal Multimodal Biospecimen Biobank for Primary CNS Lymphoma in China
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: RECRUITING] This project aims to establish and prospectively register a longitudinal, multimodal biobank for primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL). The study will primarily enroll patients undergoing needle biopsy or surgical resection of lesions involving the brain, spinal cord, or meninges, with a pathological diagnosis of central nervous system lymphoma. To ensure population homogeneity, patients with PCNSL will constitute the core analysis cohort. Patients with imaging findings suggestive of PCNSL but a final pathological diagnosis other than PCNSL will serve as disease controls, and matched healthy volunteers will be recruited as baseline controls. At baseline, biopsy tissue, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), peripheral blood, urine, saliva, and stool samples will be collected. Follow-up visits will be scheduled at 1 month after biopsy and every 3-6 months thereafter, with contrast-enhanced brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and serial collection of CSF and peripheral blood. After the requirements of routine pathological diagnosis have been met, biopsy specimens will undergo tiered multi-omics profiling according to sample availability and freshness, including whole-exome sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing, metabolomics, spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics. Analyses of CSF and blood samples will focus on circulating tumor DNA and cell-free RNA (ctDNA/cfRNA), supplemented by conventional cytology, flow cytometry, and other clinical data for longitudinal disease monitoring. The project will develop an integrated database incorporating clinical, imaging, pathological, molecular, and biospecimen data. It will characterize the relationships of baseline tissue multi-omics features and longitudinal changes in CSF- and blood-derived ctDNA/cfRNA with treatment response, recurrence prediction, and prognosis. The study will also develop diagnostic and risk-stratification models applicable to patients at our institution, across the region, and potentially throughout mainland China, while establishing standardized operating procedures for biospecimen collection and processing. This work is expected to provide high-quality evidence and a sustainable translational research platform for elucidating the biological heterogeneity of PCNSL, validating liquid-biopsy biomarkers, and optimizing precision follow-up strategies.

title: Study of Collection and Analysis of Clinical, Anamnestic, Functional, Biological Data Through the Support of Artificial Intelligence to Evaluate the Possibility of Defining a Digital Twin of the Lung (LUCE)
text: [Fase: s/d; Estado: RECRUITING] This research study aims to retrospectively and prospectively analyze the clinical, anamnestic, functional, biological data of patients who have performed or will perform non-contrast chest photon count CT. The use of contrast medium is evaluated by the physician. Main objective The study aims to understand how many people who undergo non-contrast photon-counting chest CT have: lung nodules, chest tumors, and other non-cancerous lung diseases. Secondary objectives * Analyze the data with the help of artificial intelligence to create a "digital twin" of the lung, that is, a virtual copy of the lung that allows you to study and simulate the behavior of the lung for research and analysis purposes, without directly intervening on the patient. * Follow any suspicious lung changes over time to understand how they change and whether they are linked to clinical, biological, or laboratory parameters. The enrollment phase will last 12 months and will begin with the approval of the study. At this stage, clinical data already present in the patient's medical record and data relating to the photon count CT examination will be collected. After the enrollment phase, the patient will be observed for a further total duration of 10 years: in particular, a follow-up visit will be arranged at two, five and ten years. More specifically, if there are no radiological elements that require scheduling a visit to the center, the patient will be contacted by telephone for a telematic update of the data. If, however, pulmonary alterations are identified during the study, the patient will be referred to the Reference Operating Unit, as per clinical practice, to continue with the most appropriate personalized diagnostic-therapeutic process. In these cases, the patient will be contacted by telephone and an appointment with the institution will be suggested.

title: Tumor-Specific Gene Editing Enhances Cancer Immunogenicity through Succinate Metabolism-Mediated MHC-I Reprogramming.
text: Impaired expression of major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) greatly compromises cytotoxic T-cell-mediated anticancer immunotherapy. Existing MHC-I activation strategies are greatly challenged by poor tumor specificity and off-target toxicity. Herein, we report a dual tumor-specific CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system that can precisely knock out succinate dehydrogenase subunit C (Sdhc) to activate the MHC-I pathway via epigenetic and transcriptional regulation. A tumor-specific gene editor is first engineered via reversible shielding of sgRNA using an apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1)-responsive, complementary ssDNA, yielding AP-sgRNA with blocked editing activity in normal cells yet completely restored activity in APE1-overexpressing tumor cells. Subsequently, tumor-targeted delivery of AP-sgRNA and Cas9 mRNA (mCas9) is achieved using dibenzocyclooctyne-decorated lipid nanoparticle (DLNP), which upon bioorthogonal click reaction can anchor cancer cells that are prelabeled with azido groups using the unnatural sugar DCL-AAM. Thus, AP-sgSdhc/mCas9@DLNP enables efficient and selective Sdhc editing in tumor cells, leading to epigenetic and transcriptional activation of MHC-antigen processing and presentation genes and thereby provoking robust antitumor efficacy in the B16-OVA melanoma model through enhanced, T cell-mediated immune responses. Moreover, it completely suppressed pulmonary metastasis after combination with aPD-L1 in the 4T1 lung metastasis model. This study provides an enlightened paradigm for precision gene editing and renders a promising mechanism for potentiating cancer immunotherapy.

title: Spatial Multi-Omics Integration with Mass Spectrometry Imaging: Decoding Metabolic Landscapes and Disease Mechanisms.
text: Spatial multi-omics links molecular measurements to tissue architecture, but integrating spatial transcriptomics with mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) remains challenging because the modalities differ in sampling unit, spatial resolution, data structure, and molecular-identification certainty. This review synthesizes the enabling technologies and presents an evidence-calibrated workflow spanning tissue acquisition, spatial registration, modality-specific preprocessing, cross-modal annotation, mechanistic modeling, and orthogonal validation. We examine how MSI can complement single-cell and spatial transcriptomic or proteomic measurements in studies of tumor-host interfaces, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, adipose-tissue organization, and decidualization at the maternal-fetal interface. Across these applications, spatial colocalization is most informative when annotation confidence is reported and key chemical identities are validated, registration error is quantified, and candidate cell-metabolite relationships are tested by isotope tracing or perturbation. We further discuss molecular ambiguity, resolution-sensitivity-throughput trade-offs, 3-dimensional reconstruction, interlaboratory reproducibility, and requirements for clinical translation. The central conclusion is that spatial multi-omics is best used to formulate anatomically explicit, falsifiable hypotheses rather than to infer causality from aligned maps alone.

title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
text: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of gene expression data. Additionally, PIANO achieves robust integrations and trains 10× faster than previous methods. PIANO accurately integrates single-cell data across species and across single-cell and spatial transcriptomics modalities. As practical applications, PIANO models spatially resolved gene expression during Alzheimer's disease progression in human brains and integrates over 100 million cancer cells to model drug perturbations. In summary, PIANO's integration and generative modeling capabilities will empower novel insights for a wide range of future studies.

title: From Mechanistic Models to AI Synergy: A Roadmap for Predictive and Personalized Biology.
text: Two paradigms now drive the life sciences. One is the explanatory depth of mathematical modeling, the other the predictive power of artificial intelligence. For decades, mechanistic models have offered a rigorous, hypothesis-driven framework for dissecting biological processes, while AI has proven itself at finding patterns in the large, high-dimensional datasets of modern biology. Each has delivered major advances on its own. Together they promise a synthesis that could redefine the boundaries of biological inquiry. In this review we propose a three-part taxonomy of integration strategies, namely AI-accelerated mechanistic modeling, mechanism-informed AI, and hybrid models spanning one-directional sequential coupling and bidirectional iterative systems, and we survey their applications in systems and synthetic biology, pharmacology and drug discovery, epidemiology, and neuroscience. We then examine seven challenges that stand in the way: interpretability, data sparsity, causality, identifiability, computational scale, multimodal integration, and validation and generalization, and we close with a view of biological digital twins, causal discovery engines, and automated science. Our argument is that combining these approaches is the principal task for a new generation of interdisciplinary scientists who aim to build a predictive and mechanistic science of life.

title: Nanocarrier-Mediated Immunotherapy for Gynecological Malignancies: Mechanisms, Clinical Translation, and Emerging Nucleic Acid-Based Strategies.
text: Gynecological cancers, including ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancers, remain major contributors to female morbidity and mortality worldwide. Conventional treatments-surgery, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy-have improved outcomes, but advanced or recurrent disease is still associated with poor prognosis, chemoresistance, and tumor heterogeneity. Immunotherapy has emerged as a transformative strategy because of its specificity and potential for durable responses. However, the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and inefficient delivery of immunotherapeutic agents limit clinical benefit. Nanocarriers, including organic, inorganic, and biomimetic platforms, can improve targeted delivery, sustained release, biocompatibility, and tumor microenvironment remodeling, thereby enhancing immunotherapy. This review summarizes major immunotherapeutic modalities for gynecological cancers-immune checkpoint blockade, CAR-T cell therapy, tumor vaccines, and oncolytic viruses-and the classification and characteristics of commonly used nanocarriers. We focus on nanocarrier-mediated immunotherapeutic mechanisms in ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancers, and further highlight emerging lipid nanoparticle/mRNA and programmable RNA delivery strategies. Finally, we analyze challenges in clinical translation and provide perspectives for future development, aiming to support fundamental research and clinical application of nano-immunotherapy in gynecological malignancies. Gynecological cancers are difficult to treat when they are advanced or come back after treatment. Immunotherapy can help the immune system find and attack cancer cells, but current immunotherapies often do not reach tumors well, and the tumor environment can suppress immune responses. Nanocarriers are tiny delivery systems that can carry immunotherapy drugs to tumors more precisely, protect the drugs from being cleared too quickly, and release them in a controlled way. This review explains how different nanocarriers—such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, inorganic nanoparticles, cell membrane-coated nanoparticles, virus-like particles, and exosomes—can support immunotherapy for ovarian, cervical, and endometrial cancers. We also discuss new approaches such as lipid nanoparticles and mRNA vaccines. These strategies may make immunotherapy safer, more effective, and more personalized. However, more work is needed to improve targeting, reduce long-term toxicity, scale up production, and meet regulatory requirements before these treatments can reach patients.

title: CLEAN Database: providing enzyme function coverage for over 55 million sequences.
text: Enzyme function annotation is critical for decoding biological systems and enabling rational enzyme design. However, experimentally characterized enzyme functions remain available for only a small fraction of known protein sequences, resulting in a widening gap between rapidly expanding sequence space and reliable functional assignments. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have accelerated enzyme function annotation by facilitating accurate and high-throughput prediction from protein sequences. Here, we present CLEAN Database (CLEAN DB), a comprehensive resource encompassing >55 million enzyme function annotations across 1 098 305 strains, predicted by the CLEAN AI model. The database features an intuitive web interface that enables users to efficiently search, explore, and download enzyme function data through flexible query options. Additionally, powered by a protein language model, CLEAN DB supports mutation effect prediction through interactive heatmaps, structural overlays, and tabular data visualizations. We anticipate that CLEAN DB will serve as a valuable platform for advancing enzyme discovery and applications in synthetic biology, metabolic engineering, enzyme engineering, retrosynthesis, and drug discovery. The database is freely available at https://cleandb.platform.moleculemaker.org/.

title: Pathology AI clinical integration: From promise to practice.
text: Despite substantial advances in digital and computational pathology over the past decade, pragmatic and systematic guidance for translating AI models from research into clinical practice remains limited. Most existing frameworks offer only high-level recommendations on validation, regulatory compliance, and implementation, often lacking pathology-specific roadmaps aligned with laboratory standards. This review first summarizes current progress in digitalization and AI in pathology, with emphasis on key applications in biomarker quantification, molecular status prediction, and multimodality integration. We then outline nine major components essential for pathology AI clinical integration, from defining clinical needs through analytical and clinical validation, workflow interoperability, to health economics, and further summarize and compare eight available frameworks. Next, we introduce the AI Development and Optimization in Pathology for Translation (ADOPT) framework, a practical, phased deployment roadmap specifically designed to align with College of American Pathologists and Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CAP/CLIA) guidelines, to facilitate safe and effective clinical integration of pathology AI tools. We conclude by discussing future perspectives of digital and computational pathology in cancer care, emphasizing widespread clinical adoption of digitized pathology, effective multidisciplinary collaboration, and optimized pathologist-AI synergy to fully realize the promise of pathology AI.

title: The GA4GH Workflow Execution Service: A Standard API for Workflow Execution and Management in Genomics.
text: Rapid growth in life science data generation has led to large and increasingly distributed collections of sensitive genomic data. To analyse this data, researchers increasingly rely on computational workflows to enable scalable, portable and reproducible analysis. However, these workflows are executed by specialized workflow engines across heterogeneous compute environments, each with its own requirements. As a result, users often need engine- and compute-environment-specific knowledge to submit, monitor and manage workflow execution, increasing the barriers to interoperability. These challenges are compounded in large-scale projects, where workflow runs must be dispatched to local clusters, cloud platforms or data hosting infrastructures with different underlying technologies. We describe the Global Alliance for Genomics and Health (GA4GH) Workflow Execution Service (WES) API, an approved GA4GH standard first released in 2018, together with its data model and the endpoints that define a unified interface for workflow execution. By standardizing workflow invocation, the WES API allows a single client to submit, monitor and cancel workflow runs across diverse workflow engines and compute backends, such as scheduling clusters or cloud platforms. We surveyed thirteen adoptions of the standard, covering standalone services and platforms in four programming languages. In a two-site demonstration, a WES implementation from Germany and one from Japan executed the same federated allele-frequency analysis with site-specific adjustments and only aggregated results leaving either site, demonstrating that it is possible to run the same analysis across independently built and operated WES services in different countries. From the gaps identified, we propose extensions for community discussion. The latest version of the WES API repository can be found at https://github.com/ga4gh/workflow-execution-service-schemas (DOI: https://doi.org/10.59756/m382x-ww ). The full Reference Documentation can be viewed at: https://ga4gh.github.io/workflow-execution-service-schemas/docs/. valentin.schneider-lunitz@bih-charite.de.

title: [Not Available].
text: The AIFA (Agenzia Italiana del Farmaco) monitoring registries represent one of the most distinctive regulatory tools within the Italian pharmaceutical governance framework. Initially introduced to support the appropriate use of reimbursed medicines and pharmaceutical expenditure control, they have progressively evolved into an infrastructure linking access to medicines, reimbursement governance, managed entry agreements (MEAs), and real-world data collection. This article examines the evolution and the policy relevance of AIFA monitoring registries within the Italian Health Technology Assessment framework. Firstly, it outlines the main legislative and regulatory milestones shaping the system, from the establishment of AIFA in 2003 to the publication of the 2024 guideline, which formally defined the criteria for registry activation. Secondly, it describes the main registry types, the criteria guiding their establishment, and the role of MEAs within the monitoring process. Thirdly, it provides an updated overview of the current registry landscape based on recent AIFA lists, identifying 340 closed registries (March 2026) and 366 active registries (April 2026), with “registri propriamente detti” (comprehensive registries) representing the predominant tool. Among those registries, MEAs were applied in nearly half of cases, with payment by result being the commonest scheme. The article also reviews the use of registry-derived data in peer-reviewed studies across hematology, oncology, cardiovascular diseases, and infectious diseases. Finally, it discusses key challenges, including duplication of information, limited interoperability with healthcare databases, administrative burden and residual discretion in registry activation despite recent transparency reforms. Overall, AIFA monitoring registries emerge as a strategic interface between pharmaceutical regulation, reimbursement governance, and evidence generation.

title: Artificial intelligence in odontology education.
text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored in dental education as a tool to support teaching, learning, assessment, and clinical decision-making. This systematic review synthesized current evidence on the implementation and educational impact of AI technologies in undergraduate, postgraduate, and continuing dental education. A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted using Scopus, PubMed, and IEEE Xplore. Studies published between 2020 and 2025 evaluating AI applications in dental education were identified using predefined PICO criteria. Educational outcomes included knowledge acquisition, diagnostic accuracy, clinical reasoning, procedural skills, learner engagement, and perceptions of AI-assisted learning. The included literature reflects an expansion from machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision systems primarily evaluated for diagnostic support toward generative AI platforms, including large language models and retrieval-augmented generation systems. Across the included studies, AI applications were frequently associated with favorable diagnostic and examination performance and, in selected educational contexts, with supportive findings related to clinical reasoning, technical competency, feedback, and self-directed learning. However, the evidence was predominantly based on technical performance assessments and observational or cross-sectional designs. AI is increasingly being explored as a potential complementary educational resource, with applications including interactive tutoring, adaptive learning, and support for clinical reasoning. Nevertheless, heterogeneous methodologies and limited longitudinal evidence indicate the need for standardized educational evaluation and responsible curricular integration. AI shows potential as a complementary resource in dental education. Its integration should remain pedagogically guided and ethically supervised while future research establishes its educational effectiveness through standardized and longitudinal evaluation.

title: Single-cell analysis of chromatin state and transcriptome in the human basal ganglia
text: SUMMARY The basal ganglia play essential roles in motor control, emotion, learning and reward processing. Their dysfunction contributes to many neurological and psychiatric disorders. However, the gene regulatory programs defining basal ganglia cell-type identity and function remain poorly understood, limiting interpretation of disease-associated non-coding variants. Here, we present the first single-cell multiome atlas of histone modifications and transcriptomes across eight basal ganglia regions from neurotypical adult human donors. Joint profiling reveals cell-type-specific deployment of active and repressive cis -regulatory elements and gene regulatory networks, and suggests a combinatorial homeobox transcription factor code underlying cell identity. Integration with matched spatial transcriptomic MERFISH data uncovers regional heterogeneity of epigenomic landscapes. Comparative analysis between human and mouse medium spiny neurons uncovers conservation of core gene regulatory features. This atlas interprets non-coding risk variants of neuropsychiatric disorders and supports the development of a deep learning model to predict gene regulation and functional effects of disease-associated variants. HIGHLIGHTS Joint single-cell profiling of transcriptomes and three histone modifications across eight human basal ganglia regions characterizes active and repressive chromatin states at cell-type resolution. Cell-type-specific gene regulatory programs decode combinatorial homeobox TF grammar governing the identity and diversification of basal ganglia neurons. Intergrative analyses link noncoding neuropsychiatric risk variants to specific cell types, regulatory elements, and candidate target genes. A sequence-to-function deep-learning model predicts gene regulation from DNA sequence and prioritizes functional disease-associated variants.

title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
text: Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

title: MASLD-Mitochondrial Digital Twin: Mapping mitonuclear epistasis to predict disease trajectory and systemic bioenergetic homeostasis
text: Abstract Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent chronic disorder with marked clinical heterogeneity and divergent outcomes. Current pathophysiological models fail to fully account for inter-individual variation in progression toward steatohepatitis and systemic multimorbidity. This Perspective posits the mitochondrion as an integrative functional hub where genomic predisposition, epigenomic plasticity, and bioenergetic signaling converge to shape the disease's longitudinal trajectory. We synthesize evidence from the mitonuclear interactome—the co-evolutionary and functional coordination between nuclear and mitochondrial genomes, hepatic epigenomic remodeling, and circulating mitochondrial metabotypes to propose a unified systems biology framework: the MASLD-Mitochondrial Digital Twin (MASLD-MDT). This multiscale platform integrates high-resolution biological data—including single-cell mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) heteroplasmy, NAD+ redox dynamics, and the systemic efflux of mitochondrial-derived peptides (MDPs)—to simulate individualized disease kinetics. By reframing MASLD as a systemic mitochondriopathy, the MASLD-MDT could quantify critical bioenergetic thresholds, providing a novel metric for risk stratification and the in silico optimization of therapeutic deployment. This hypothesis-oriented instrument aims to advance the field toward a mitochondrial precision medicine strategy, enabling the discovery of targeted interventions to intercept multi-organ compromise.

title: Cognitive digital twins: A state-of-the-art review
text: Digital twins are a key enabling technology for Industry 4.0/5.0 that provide digital representations of physical systems for monitoring and decision-making support. However, the increasing complexity, autonomy, and connectivity of modern industrial systems challenge traditional digital twin approaches focused on simple replication. Therefore, advanced capabilities that go beyond mirroring physical assets are required to enable simulation, optimization, prediction, and adaptive behavior. Cognitive digital twins extend the capabilities of traditional digital twins by integrating cognitive functions such as perception, attention, memory, reasoning, problem-solving, and learning through artificial intelligence techniques, including machine learning. This review considers the differences between cognitive and traditional digital twins, and investigates the operationalization of cognitive functions. It examines how algorithms, software, tools, and frameworks are implemented for cognitive digital twins through a systematic literature review conducted using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methodology. Moreover, it identifies current advancements; maps cognitive functions to applications; highlights underrepresented functions and implementation gaps in interoperability, validation, and learning infrastructure; and establishes opportunities for standardized evaluation and modular cross-sector designs.

title: Principal Decomposition with Nested Submanifolds
text: Summary Over the past decades, the increasing dimensionality of data has increased the need for effective data decomposition methods. Existing approaches, however, often rely on linear models or lack sufficient interpretability or flexibility. To address this issue, we introduce a novel nonlinear decomposition technique called the principal nested submanifolds, which builds on the foundational concepts of principal component analysis. This method exploits the local geometric information of data sets by projecting samples onto a series of nested principal submanifolds with progressively decreasing dimensions. It effectively isolates complex information within the data in a backward stepwise manner by targeting variations associated with smaller eigenvalues in local covariance matrices. The fitted structures are smooth nested manifolds rather than linear or special-shape subspaces. Simulation studies and an analysis of single-cell RNA-sequencing data illustrate how the method summarizes locally varying nonlinear structure while retaining a compatible hierarchy across dimensions. It provides flexible subspace constraints that facilitate the extraction of data components and noise reduction. This approach advances the non-Euclidean statistical analysis of data with low-dimensional intrinsic structure within Euclidean spaces and offers a complementary perspective for high-dimensional noisy data sets in fields such as bioinformatics and machine learning.

title: Microbial CO2 bioconversion: integrating carbon fixation pathways and sustainable biomanufacturing
text: The continued rise in atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) concentrations has intensified the need for sustainable technologies capable of mitigating greenhouse gas emissions while generating value-added products. In this context, microbial CO 2 bioconversion has emerged as a promising biological strategy within broader carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) frameworks, particularly through biological carbon capture and utilization (bio-CCU). These approaches enable the conversion of inorganic carbon into fuels, chemicals, biomaterials, proteins, and other value-added products. This review provides a comprehensive assessment of recent advances in microbial CO 2 bioconversion by bridging biological, technological, and industrial perspectives. Unlike previous reviews focusing on individual topics, such as carbon fixation pathways, gas fermentation, or metabolic engineering, this work presents an integrated framework connecting natural and synthetic carbon fixation pathways, microbial production platforms, metabolic engineering strategies, product diversification, and techno-economic considerations. To support this analysis, we conducted a systematic bibliometric assessment of 913 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, revealing sustained growth in scientific output, increasing interdisciplinarity, structured collaboration networks, and strong thematic interconnections across microbial ecology, carbon fixation, metabolism, and carbon utilization. Recent advances in synthetic biology, systems-level metabolic engineering, microbial electrosynthesis, bioelectrochemical systems, synthetic microbial consortia, and artificial intelligence-assisted strain engineering are discussed as important drivers of microbial carbon utilization. The review also critically examines major barriers to industrial implementation, including CO 2 mass transfer, carbon fixation efficiency, energy constraints, process scale-up, downstream processing, and economic feasibility. By integrating systematic bibliometric evidence with a critical assessment of microbial CO 2 biomanufacturing, this review identifies the convergence of microbial physiology, metabolic engineering, bioprocess development, renewable energy, and data-driven approaches as central to advancing biological CO 2 conversion toward scalable, sustainable biomanufacturing.

title: Multiparameter Optimization Extends the Lifetime of Cell-Free Protein Synthesis in a High-Throughput Format
text: Abstract Cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) is a powerful platform for synthetic biology, yet the factors governing reaction longevity remain poorly understood despite their importance for high-throughput applications. Here, the three principal determinants of CFPS performanceDNA template design, reaction composition, and lysate genotypewere systematically optimized to extend reaction lifetime in a 384-well plate format. Different energy regeneration systems were evaluated through real-time pH monitoring and metabolomic analyses to identify the metabolic constraints limiting prolonged protein synthesis. Lysates prepared from engineered Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) strains were further examined to assess the contributions of DNA, RNA, and amino acid stabilization. Systematic optimization of amino acid, nucleoside triphosphate, polyethylene glycol, and lysate concentrations identified DNA template stability and amino acid preservation as the primary factors sustaining CFPS activity. Combining these improvements yielded reactions that remained productive for >14 h and produced 567 ± 64 μg mL−1 active deGFP. These findings establish practical strategies for extending CFPS lifetime and improving high-throughput cell-free platforms.
