title: A Prospective Trial of SFI Plus PD-1 Inhibitors and PBC in Resectable NSCLC (SFI-NSCLC)
text: [Fase: PHASE4; Estado: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] This prospective, single-center clinical trial will enroll 30 treatment-naïve patients with locally advanced, resectable stage II-IIIA non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) to receive neoadjuvant Shenqi Fuzheng Injection (SFI) in combination with a PD-1 inhibitor and platinum-based chemotherapy. The primary endpoint is the pathological complete response (pCR) rate, while secondary endpoints include the major pathological response (MPR) rate and event-free survival (EFS). Furthermore, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics will be employed to dynamically track alterations in the immune regulatory network within the tumor microenvironment (TME) pre- and post-SFI administration. This approach aims to elucidate how SFI remodels the TME immune landscape and to uncover its potential advantages in improving clinical outcomes. Additionally, we will investigate the synergistic effects of SFI combined with PD-1 blockade and platinum-based chemotherapy, with the ultimate goal of advancing the integration of traditional Chinese medicine into the therapeutic paradigm for resectable NSCLC.

title: WHO guidance helps detect iron deficiency and protect brain development
text: Detecting iron deficiency early during pregnancy and in young children is crucial. Iron deficiency in children under two years of age can have significant and irreversible effects on brain development. This can lead to negative consequences on learning and school performance later in life. Cognitive development of a child can also be affected if a mother is iron deficient during her last trimester of pregnancy. New World Health Organization guidelines on the use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status in individuals and populations will help health workers to detect iron deficiency early and avoid the most severe impacts.  WHO shows how to best measure ferritin, an indicator of iron stores, to help determine iron deficiency or overload. Ferritin is a protein which can be found in small amounts circulating in a person’s blood. Ferritin levels are low in iron-deficient individuals and high in iron-loaded individuals. Accurate measurements of this protein, along with clinical and laboratory evaluation, can guide the appropriate interventions in both individual patients and at a population level. “Reducing anemia is one of the components of our efforts to eradicate all forms of malnutrition. However, progress has been limited and we still have 614 million women and 280 million children globally who suffer from it,” said Dr Francesco Branca, Director of the Department of Nutrition and Food Safety at WHO. “Iron deficiency is a major determinant of anemia and measuring ferritin, a key biomarker of iron metabolism, will help us better target and evaluate our action to fight anemia” Iron is an essential element with important functions such as oxygen transport, DNA synthesis and muscle metabolism. Iron deficiency is the main cause of anaemia, which is the most prevalent nutritional deficiency worldwide, affecting 33% of non-pregnant women, 40% of pregnant women, and 42% of children worldwide. In adults, iron deficiency can also have negative effects including fatigue, impaired physical performance and decreased work productivity, as well as impacting social activities. Iron deficiency occurs mainly when the requirements of iron increase during rapid periods of growth and development such as in early childhood, adolescence and pregnancy, but it can occur at other stages in life. In pregnant women, iron deficiency can cause anaemia, reduced birth weight and reduced gestation periods. The new guidelines also cover the early detection of iron overload. Iron overload (accumulation of iron in the body) is generally the result of disorders such as hereditary haemochromatosis, thalassaemia, repeated blood transfusions or other conditions that affect iron absorption or regulation and can also lead to deterioration of a person’s health if left untreated. Improved knowledge about the prevalence and distribution of iron deficiency and risk of iron overload in the population helps countries to decide on appropriate interventions, and to monitor and evaluate the impact and safety of public health programmes. For example, nutritional iron deficiency can be commonly found in populations that also have infectious diseases. The adequate evaluation of iron status in countries with infectious disorders can help countries to put in place adequate health policies. The WHO guidelines aim to help WHO Member States and their partners to make evidence-informed decisions on appropriate actions in their efforts to lower iron deficiency and improve the health and quality of life of individuals and populations. For interviews with WHO technical experts, please contact: Pippa HAUGHTON – haughtonp@who.int +41794466331 To access a copy of the full guidelines, please visit

title: CRISPR opens the door to targeted therapy against glioblastoma (Review).
text: The progression in molecular understanding of glioblastoma (GBM) enables the identification of key therapeutic targets, allowing the advances of targeted therapy in GBM. However, to date, most clinical trial results have been disappointing. The clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) system is a revolutionary genome‑editing tool that has the potential to improve basic research and therapy for GBM. In the present review, the current status and challenges of targeted therapy in GBM are examined. As a potential approach to address the challenges, the development process and application scope of CRISPR are investigated. Furthermore, the application of CRISPR in the study of GBM is explored, mainly by conducting CRISPR screens and employing CRISPR to target genes associated with the malignant phenotype of GBM. Finally, delivery of CRISPR/CRISPR‑associated protein 9 (Cas9) for the treatment of GBM is briefly reviewed.

title: AAV8-mediated CasRx delivery and expression in the cochlea and cochlear nucleus of mice.
text: CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing has made substantial progress in recent years and has enabled the treatment of a variety of genetic diseases, including hearing loss in congenitally deaf mice. However, successful gene editing for hereditary deafness may still induce off-target mutations in genomic DNA, which limits its clinical translation. CasRx, also known as RfxCas13d, is a compact RNA-targeting CRISPR effector that can be packaged into AAV vectors for in vivo delivery. CasRx, a recently identified member of the type VI CRISPR system, modulates target RNA expression without altering DNA sequences, thereby avoiding permanent off-target mutations and offering broad therapeutic potential. Here, we used adeno-associated virus serotype 8 (AAV8) to deliver CasRx into the cochlea and cochlear nucleus (CN) of C57BL/6J mice and evaluated its expression pattern and short-term safety. Two weeks after viral injection, the number and morphology of neurons and other cell types in the CN remained normal. Importantly, auditory brainstem response (ABR) thresholds were unchanged after viral delivery, indicating that AAV8-mediated CasRx expression did not detectably impair auditory function during the short observation period. In conclusion, this study demonstrates the feasibility and short-term safety of AAV8-mediated CasRx delivery and expression in the cochlea and cochlear nucleus, providing a delivery platform for future guide RNA-directed transcript-modulation studies in auditory disorders.

title: S100A4 facilitates influenza A virus replication by interacting with M2 in human alveolar epithelial cells.
text: Influenza A virus (IAV) replication depends on host cells and is regulated by numerous host factors. Therefore, investigating and understanding the role of these host factors is a significant topic. In this study, we found the IAV replication was attenuated after host factor S100 calcium-binding protein A4 (S100A4) was knocked down with RNAi or knockout with CRISPR/Cas9 gene-editing technology. Conversely, IAV replication was enhanced upon the overexpression in A549 cells. The interaction between S100A4 and the IAV M2 protein was confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation. Meanwhile, confocal microscopy experiment demonstrated that the viral M2 protein co-localized with endogenous S100A4 in IAV-infected A549 cells. Truncation analysis confirmed that amino acids 45-62 of the M2 protein constitute the main interaction region with S100A4. Further study showed that viral entry was reduced after S100A4 deletion. And the polymerase activity was significantly decreased in S100A4-knockout A549 cells compared to that in wild-type A549 cells. The S100A4 overexpression resulted in the downregulation of IFN-β, while the mRNA levels of the interferon-stimulated genes ISG15 and BST2 were also significantly reduced. Therefore, the host factor S100A4 was a positive modulator of IAV replication and was involved in the viral entry, polymerase activity maintenance and innate immune regulation. Collectively, our findings shed new light on the molecular mechanisms governing IAV infection and suggest a previously underexplored avenue for antiviral therapeutic intervention.

title: Microbiome-guided rhizosphere engineering for sustainable remediation of agricultural soil contaminants.
text: Agricultural soils increasingly carry mixtures of pesticide residues, heavy metals, petroleum hydrocarbons and microplastics, and conventional phytoremediation is too slow and too contaminant-specific to address them. Rhizosphere engineering, the deliberate manipulation of root-associated microbial communities, is widely proposed as the alternative, but the literature reports laboratory, pot and field results in a single register, so a reader cannot easily tell which approaches are deployable. This mini-review stratifies that evidence rather than surveying it. Every approach examined is assigned to one of three tiers: field-validated, emerging at pot or microcosm scale, or conceptual. Only two domains prove to be field-validated, namely metal immobilization and phytoextraction through bioaugmentation and bulk amendment, and hydrocarbon rhizoremediation by defined consortia; both rest on cultured isolates rather than engineered organisms. Microplastic rhizoremediation has not been demonstrated in soil, and we separate interception, adsorption, weathering, transformation and mineralization to show why reported removal is usually not degradation. Synthetic biology, CRISPR-based community editing and computational design remain conceptual, and we set out the horizontal gene transfer, containment, non-target and regulatory obstacles that stand between them and field use. We identify the measurements that would move an approach from one tier to the next, and argue that the principal deficit in this field is not technical capability but field-scale evidence reported to a common standard.

title: Virus-like particles enable highly efficient gene editing across porcine and avian in vitro, ex vivo, and in ovo models.
text: Pigs and chickens are not only the most important livestock species for global food production but also serve as key model organisms in various research disciplines. The pig is widely used in translational research due to its anatomical and physiological similarity to humans, providing valuable insights into immunology, metabolism, and disease mechanisms. In contrast, the chicken has become an essential model for studies related to poultry health, animal welfare, and developmental biology. Its externally developing embryo offers exceptional accessibility for experimental manipulation. Recent advances in genome editing technologies, particularly CRISPR/Cas9, have further expanded the potential of these species for functional genomic studies, although the efficient delivery of such tools remains a major challenge. Here, we overcome this delivery limitation by using virus-like particles (VLPs). We evaluated VLPs as delivery vehicles for genome engineering tools in porcine and avian cultures, two key livestock species at the human-animal interface. VLP-mediated delivery enabled efficient Cre recombination and high CRISPR/Cas9 editing rates in porcine cells, organoids, and oocytes, particularly when multiplexed. In chickens, VLPs supported robust Cre recombination and Cas9-mediated editing in cell culture, tracheal organ cultures, and in ovo. Reporter VLPs and dCas9 VLPs further demonstrated the versatility of this platform across porcine and avian systems. Together, these findings establish VLPs as an efficient and time-saving strategy for gene editing in livestock cultures across in vitro, ex vivo and in ovo systems, with potential future applications for animal health, agricultural productivity, and translational One Health research.

title: Mapping Osteosarcoma Biology With CRISPR/Cas: From Gene Function to Therapeutic Targets.
text: Osteosarcoma is a highly aggressive primary bone malignancy characterized by rapid proliferation, chemoresistance, and early metastasis. Recent advances in CRISPR/Cas (clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats/CRISPR-associated proteins) genome editing have enabled precise targeting of oncogenes, tumor suppressors, and regulators of epigenetic, metabolic, and signaling pathways, providing new insights into osteosarcoma biology. CRISPR-mediated knockout of cell-cycle regulators, including CDK11, impairs proliferation, while restoration of TP53 and suppression of TERT promoter activity inhibits tumor growth. Other line of studies has revealed that chemoresistance mechanisms mediated by ABCB1/MDR1, CD44, ATR, RAD18, and autophagy-related genes have been effectively reversed through CRISPR interventions, restoring sensitivity to cisplatin and doxorubicin. Furthermore, CRISPR applications in immune modulation, such as PD-L1 knockout, may enhance antitumor immunity. Importantly, high-throughput CRISPR screens also may identify essential genes, novel oncogenic drivers, and synthetic lethal targets, thus informing potential precision therapeutic strategies. This review aims to critically summarize CRISPR/Cas-mediated studies in osteosarcoma, focusing on targeting oncogenes and tumor suppressors, overcoming chemoresistance, modulating immune responses, regulating metabolism and autophagy, and identifying essential genes and vulnerabilities, providing a translational framework for precision therapy.

title: Comprehensive characterization of the cellular and molecular consequences of LCN2 loss in MDA-MB-231 triple-negative breast cancer cells.
text: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive breast cancer subtype characterized by high metastatic potential and limited targeted therapeutic options. Lipocalin-2 (LCN2) has been implicated in tumor progression and metastatic dissemination, but its functional role in TNBC remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the role of LCN2 in the human TNBC cell line MDA-MB-231. Stable LCN2-deficient (LCN2KO) cells were generated using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, followed by isolation of single-cell-derived clones. RNA sequencing was performed to characterize transcriptomic changes, with selected findings validated by reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Western blotting was used to assess protein-level changes. Transwell migration and invasion assays and adhesion assays were performed to evaluate functional effects. LCN2KO cells largely retained the mesenchymal phenotype of parental cells. RNA sequencing revealed changes associated with inflammatory signaling, iron homeostasis, oxidative stress, ferroptosis-related processes, and cellular metabolism. Functional assays demonstrated reduced migration, invasion, and adhesion, accompanied by altered adhesion to extracellular matrix components. LCN2 deficiency is associated with transcriptional and functional changes in MDA-MB-231 cells, particularly affecting migratory and invasive behavior and cell-matrix interactions, while largely preserving the mesenchymal phenotype. These findings provide further insight into the role of LCN2 in cellular processes relevant to TNBC progression and metastatic behavior.

title: ASAOT: an accentuated structure-differentiated asymmetric optimal transport model for cell type and single-cell spatial mapping.
text: Spatial transcriptomics (STs) characterizes spatiotemporal gene expression and facilitates analysis of cellular architecture and cell-cell crosstalk within tissue microenvironments. However, existing spatial deconvolution methods employ globally fixed smoothing without local sharpening, which blurs cellular boundaries and impedes reconstruction of layered, heterogeneous cellular patterns in brain tissue. Here, we present Accentuated Structure-differentiated Asymmetric Optimal Transport (ASAOT), a deconvolution framework built on structure-enhanced asymmetric optimal transport. Coupled with spatial neighborhood constraints, ASAOT introduces a differentiated accentuated sharpening term to maintain global spatial continuity, enhance boundary detection, and preserve spot-level expression heterogeneity. Using asymmetric optimal transport, the framework jointly estimates spot-wise cell-type proportions and performs spatial assignment of reference single-cell coordinates. Benchmarks on diverse simulated datasets demonstrate that ASAOT achieves competitive overall accuracy and robustness across moderate spatial resolutions, with the best average comprehensive rank among tested methods. Applications to mouse olfactory bulb and cerebral cortex datasets demonstrate that ASAOT reduces signal diffusion and boundary distortion, effectively recovering layered brain anatomy and stratified cell distributions to build interpretable spatial maps of reference single-cell profiles. Collectively, ASAOT addresses critical drawbacks of conventional methods via a sharpening regularization term, serving as a reliable tool for STs analysis and mechanism exploration of tissue spatial organization.

title: Cell-Cell Communication Network Analysis of Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
text: Tertiary Lymphoid Structures (TLS) are associated with a favorable prognosis in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC). However, the mechanisms governing their formation, particularly the existence of breast cancer subtype-specific critical cell communication networks, remain unclear. This study aims to systematically decipher the specific cellular interaction networks associated with TLS in TNBC and Estrogen Receptor-positive Breast Cancer (ER+ BC). Public spatial transcriptomics (TNBC: GSE210616; ER+ BC: 10x Genomics public Visium dataset) and single-cell transcriptomics (GSE176078) data were integrated to attribute TLS-associated genes to their cell-type origins and infer intercellular communication. TLS regions were independently identified by two pathologists based on H&E images (TNBC: 7 TLS; ER+ BC: 12 TLS), followed by differential expression analysis. Using single-cell data, a dual-criterion (expression rate ≥20% and average expression level ≥ upper quartile) was employed for cell-type expression attribution, with sensitivity analysis across thresholds. Cell-cell communication network inference and quantitative analysis were performed based on an expanded ligand-receptor database (CellTalkDB, 3,398 pairs), and the core findings were cross-validated using CellChat. TLS in TNBC exhibited a far more active transcriptional state compared to ER+ Breast Cancer (ER+ BC), with 198 vs 29 differentially expressed genes. Interaction network analysis revealed that in TNBC TLS, fibroblasts (cancer-associated fibroblasts, CAFs) constituted the dominant core signaling hub (net signal output strength: +458.7), whereas endothelial cells were the predominant net signal receiver (net output: -808.6). In contrast, TLS in ER+ BC were characterized by interactions predominantly involving fibroblasts (dominant output, +261.1) and plasma cells (dominant reception, -127.0). Cell-type expression attribution further confirmed that TLS-associated signals in TNBC predominantly originated from fibroblasts (70.3% of core TLS genes). Our intercellular communication analysis reveals a stark subtype-specific landscape: TLSs in TNBC are predominantly characterized by a fibroblast (CAF)-centered signaling hub, whereas TLS in ER+ BC features a fibroblast-plasma cell axis. The association between the TLS-related transcriptional signature and immune cytolytic activity was further supported in the independent The Cancer Genome Atlas breast cancer cohort (r = 0.747, P < 0.001). However, as these inferences are drawn from transcriptional correlations in public datasets, further mechanistic studies-such as ligand-receptor functional assays or in vivo perturbation models-are essential to determine whether this TNBC-specific hub actively contributes to TLS formation or merely reflects the local immune microenvironment. This study identifies a TNBC-specific fibroblast (CAF)-centered communication hub as a prominent feature of TLS-associated intercellular networks, offering prioritized candidate axes warranting further functional validation for potential immunotherapy development.

title: Software-based concordance analysis of a predictive surgical planning model for target gap achievement in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
text: In robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA), achieving soft-tissue balance requires repeated intraoperative plan adjustment and remains experience-dependent. Predictive models may support planning, but their clinical value depends on whether model-generated plans approximate predefined target gaps within the robotic workflow. This study assessed the software-based concordance between model-generated plans and predefined target gaps in robotic-assisted TKA. The predefined target gaps were planning set points established within the robotic software rather than measured intraoperative gaps. This retrospective software-based concordance study included 209 complete-case knees undergoing robotic-assisted TKA. A machine-learning-based predictive model generated a bone-resection plan, which was imported into the robotic planning software to calculate software-derived medial and lateral gaps in extension and flexion. These software-derived gaps were compared with predefined target gaps, which were planning set points rather than measured values and were 18 mm in 819 of 836 gap-level observations (98.0%). The primary analysis focused on target gap deviation, defined as the software-derived gap minus the predefined target gap. As a benchmark, the deviation of the preadjustment gaps from the same targets was used as a preadjustment reference. A total of 836 gap-level observations were analyzed. The overall mean target gap deviation was -0.142 mm (SD, 1.411 mm), with a mean absolute error of 1.016 mm. Overall, 77.6% of software-derived gaps were within ±1 mm of target, and 93.4% were within ±2 mm. Bland-Altman analysis showed a small overall bias of -0.142 mm, with 95% limits of agreement from -2.91 to +2.62 mm. At the knee level, only 43.1% of knees had all software-derived gaps within ±1 mm of target. Gap-level deviations ranged from -7 mm to +5 mm, and 16.3% of knees (34/209) had at least one gap with an absolute deviation > 2 mm. Compared with the preadjustment reference (MAE 2.002 mm, 49.4% within ±1 mm), the model substantially reduced deviation (MAE 1.016 mm, 77.6% within ±1 mm, p < 0.001). In this software-based concordance analysis, the predictive planning model generated surgical plans whose robotic software-derived gaps approximated predefined target gaps with a mean absolute deviation of approximately 1 mm. The model-generated plan reduced target-gap deviation relative to the initial preadjustment plan within this target-conditioned workflow. However, because the targets were near-uniform (98.0% at 18 mm) and all measurements were software-derived, compartment-specific bias, moderate whole-knee consistency (43.1%), and occasional outlier deviations indicate that the model should be used as a surgeon-supervised decision support tool rather than as an autonomous planner. Prospective validation against measured intraoperative and postoperative gaps is required before clinical effectiveness can be claimed.

title: Development of a Digital Twin to Analyse Waiting Lists in a Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit.
text: This study developed and validated a digital twin of patient flow and waiting list dynamics in a Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit, based on a discrete-event simulation (DES) model in the context of growing diagnostic demand mainly driven by obstructive sleep apnoea. The stochastic model, implemented in MATLAB, reproduces six care stages (e-Consultation, face-to-face consultation, overnight pulse oximetry, respiratory polygraphy, polysomnography and follow-up consultation), using operational data from year 2024 for parameterisation and data from year 2025 for correlation and validation. Key performance indicators included mean waiting time and mean queue length per stage, with model fidelity assessed via Mean Absolute Error, Root Mean Squared Error and Relative Percent Difference (RPD), both by stage and globally across the full patient pathway. The model accurately reproduced the aggregate system workload, with a weighted RPD of 3.6% for mean queue length and 34.6% for mean waiting time. Respiratory polygraphy showed the best agreement in terms of service load (RPD 2.7%), whereas the follow-up consultation exhibited the largest discrepancies in waiting times (RPD 73.7%), likely related to prioritisation rules and organisational variability not explicitly modelled. Overall, this digital twin provides an operationally useful representation to support 'what-if' analyses of organisational scenarios aimed at reducing diagnostic delays, representing one of the first validated applications of DES model in a dedicated Sleep-Disordered Breathing Unit and provides a basis for future applications incorporating urgency stratification and prospective analysis.

title: Gadoxetic acid in China: a narrative review of the 15-year journey and the road ahead.
text: Since its pivotal introduction in 2011, gadoxetic acid has fundamentally revolutionized the landscape of hepatobiliary imaging in China, shifting the diagnostic paradigm from morphological assessment toward functional hepatocyte-level evaluation. This review comprehensively summarizes its 15-year clinical evolution within the Chinese healthcare system, exploring its pharmacological benefits, advanced applications, and future integration with data-driven frameworks. A systematic literature search was conducted across major electronic databases, including PubMed, Web of Science, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure, spanning from 2011 to 2026. The search targeted peer-reviewed articles, consensus statements, clinical guidelines, and high-impact reviews published in English and Chinese regarding gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Gadoxetic acid provides high sensitivity for early small hepatocellular carcinoma (sHCC) detection via specific OATP1B3 uptake. Beyond lesion detection, its quantitative mapping shows potential for estimating hepatic functional reserve (HFR) and risk stratification for post-hepatectomy liver failure. Crucially, the ongoing paradigm shift toward integrating radiomics and deep learning bridges macroscopic imaging and microscopic molecular biology, theoretically enabling a multi-dimensional profile of liver parenchyma and lesions within a single diagnostic session. However, a significant gap remains between retrospective predictive performance and clinical readiness, and these data-driven frameworks currently serve as supplementary investigational engines rather than standalone clinical decision-makers. Moving forward, integrating these high-dimensional signatures into constructs such as "digital twin" represents the next frontier. Furthermore, China's hepatitis B virus-dominant epidemiological cohorts, comprehensive multi-modal datasets, "Med-Engineering" fusion, and collaborative networks uniquely accelerate the development and preliminary validation of these models, offering valuable insights for global precision hepatology within China's healthcare system. Over the past 15 years, gadoxetic acid has evolved far beyond a conventional liver imaging tool in China. While clinical translation of advanced analytics requires rigorous, prospective multicenter validation to ensure safety, combining this functional imaging agent with data-driven frameworks represents a promising frontier to eventually optimize future radiology workflows and support personalized precision hepatology.

title: Programmable RNA therapeutics: converging vaccination and on-demand disease treatment via self-adaptive RNA platforms.
text: RNA technology, most prominently messenger RNA (mRNA), has transformed vaccine development by enabling rapid, sequence-specific antigen design, scalable manufacturing, and transient protein expression. Its long-term significance, however, extends beyond prophylactic vaccination. This Perspective argues that mRNA should be conceptualised as a programmable therapeutic platform capable of integrating vaccination, immune modulation, and on-demand disease treatment. Current mRNA vaccines deliver predefined antigenic instructions, whereas emerging RNA systems, including self-amplifying RNA (saRNA), circular RNA, sequence-engineered mRNA, and targeted lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), may support more adaptable therapeutic functions. Such platforms could prime immunity, replace deficient proteins, encode antibodies, reprogramme immune cells, or induce antigen-specific tolerance. The concept of self-adaptive RNA-based therapeutics remains at an early stage and should not be overstated; most existing systems are programmable at the design stage rather than biologically autonomous after administration. Nonetheless, this conceptual position is no longer purely speculative: the first regulatory approval of a self-amplifying RNA vaccine and controlled-trial evidence of clinical benefit from a personalised neoantigen mRNA therapeutic in resected melanoma indicate that programmable RNA platforms are beginning to move from concept to clinical validation across both the prophylactic and therapeutic ends of the spectrum. Key challenges include tissue-specific delivery, expression control, innate immune activation, repeat dosing, safety assessment, regulatory classification, and equitable access. A self-adaptive RNA-based framework does not replace existing vaccines or biologics but extends them towards responsive, personalised, and temporally controlled therapy.

title: A field-deployable colorimetric reverse transcription-LAMP assay for the detection of a prostate cancer biomarker.
text: Prostate cancer (PCa) is becoming increasingly common in males worldwide, and early identification is crucial for improved patient prognosis and therapeutic results. Messenger ribonucleic acids (mRNAs) are promising noninvasive biomarkers for PCa diagnosis because they can be extracted from various body fluids. Yes-Associated Protein 1 (YAP1) mRNA is a biomarker for PCa diagnosis and is highly expressed in human PCa cells. Herein, the ability of RT-LAMP and a visual platform to detect YAP1 mRNA for PCa diagnosis was explored. For the first time, the color behavior of a charge-transfer complex (oxTMB) was investigated to detect a PCa biomarker. Due to the electrostatic interactions between the positively-charged oxTMB and the negatively-charged LAMP amplicons, oxTMB was not reduced even when the potential reductant, dopamine (DA), was added. Consequently, the green color of oxTMB was retained under electrostatic interactions, whereas oxTMB in the negative sample was reduced, and the green color disappeared. The introduced oxTMB/DA-based LAMP approach showed high selectivity and a visual limit of detection of the PCa biomarker at 3.64 × 104 copies/μL in a cultured DU-145 cell line-derived RNA sample. Owing to its simplicity, rapidity, and practical viability, this oxTMB/DA-based colorimetric approach could be employed to detect PCa biomarkers in resource-limited areas.

title: Discovery, identification of tricyclic sesquiterpene avermitilol synthase, and its heterologous production in plasmid-free Corynebacterium glutamicum.
text: Tricyclic sesquiterpenes are bioactive natural products with broad applications in pharmaceuticals, fragrances, and sustainable aviation biofuels. However, the repertoire of characterized tricyclic sesquiterpene synthases (tSTSs) remains limited. To systematically expand this enzyme class, we developed a multi-step bioinformatics workflow to identify genes encoding for cyclic sesquiterpene synthase integrating BLAST-based homology filtering, conserved motif validation, AlphaFold2-based structural modeling, and molecular docking. This workflow progressively refined an initial set of 1063 tSTS candidates to six putative enzymes that satisfied a C1-C10 distance criterion. Heterologous expression of all six candidates in Corynebacterium glutamicum JP-2 overexpressing a methylerythritol 4-phosphate pathway gene module confirmed biosynthetic activity, yielding five known cyclic sesquiterpenes and tricyclic avermitilol produced by a tSTS (AtTPS) identified from Actinokineospora terrae by NMR spectroscopy and high-resolution electrospray ionization mass spectrometry. To improve industrial feasibility, the chemical-inducible promoter was replaced with constitutive leaderless synthetic σB promoters, and fusion of avermitilol synthase with farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase via a GGGGS linker enhanced the local concentration of intermediates between enzymes. In addition, a plasmid-free, antibiotic selection-free strain was constructed via the CRISPR-associated transposons, enabling dual chromosomal integrations of the avermitilol synthase expression cassette and achieving 81.52 mg/L avermitilol production. The chromosomally integrated strain maintained stable production over serial passages, whereas the plasmid-based strain exhibited greater than 90% loss of productivity. Fed-batch fermentation of AVM-int02cp in a 2-L bioreactor achieved a final avermitilol titer of 100.99 mg/L. This work demonstrates a sequence- and 3D structure-assisted gene discovery-to-production workflow for a tricyclic sesquiterpene through the identification of an uncharacterized synthase gene in a microbial host.

title: Pan-Canadian health workforce data sources: Bridging the divides to better inform research, policy and planning.
text: High-quality data on the health workforce are needed for effective health workforce research, policy and planning in support of care delivery and system strengthening. Standardized data in uniquely decentralized health systems makes it possible to understand overall supply, distribution and mobility trends across jurisdictions and to inform international benchmarking. To describe two key pan-Canadian health workforce data sources, identifying key challenges and opportunities for optimizing data for research, policy and planning. We conducted a multi-phase environmental scan: (1) mapping CIHI and Statistics Canada data holdings and collection methods; (2) reviewing 2015-2025 literature to assess their use, strengths, and gaps; and (3) comparing sources to identify discrepancies and implications for pan-Canadian workforce analysis and planning. Two data pan-Canadian custodians - the Canadian Institute for Health Information and Statistics Canada - collate health workforce data from health administrative sources and undertake population census, labour force, education and health-focused surveys respectively. Both custodians maintain datasets that reflect the breadth and depth of health workforce information. Neither source is designed primarily to inform health workforce planning, resulting in variability in the coverage of professions and policy-relevant topics. Despite the policy priority of interprofessional collaboration, when data are used for health workforce analysis it remains focused on a single sector or profession reflective of data silos and divergent standardization. Targeted investments into data development, standardization and interoperability are key areas for enhancing interprofessional and cross-jurisdictional health workforce policy and planning.

title: When Systems Talk-Measuring Neurology Care in the Digital Era: Emerging Issues in Neurology.
text: Neurology is entering a decade in which rapid growth in diagnostic technologies, data streams, and care delivery models collides with persistent fragmentation of neurologic information across electronic health records, imaging systems, and remote monitoring platforms. As these data sources proliferate, interoperability has emerged as a foundational requirement for high-quality neurologic care. The current landscape limits longitudinal understanding of disease trajectories, impedes care transitions, burdens quality measurement, and constrains research. This article articulates the current and future challenges of interoperability for neurology by characterizing the current state of interoperability; surveying relevant national standards and platforms; identifying key technical, semantic, and organizational barriers; and proposing future goals for improving interoperable neurologic care. Part and parcel of these challenges and goals are the evolving regulatory and policy frameworks, including the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement, provisions of the 21st Century Cures Act, and federal interoperability rules that mandate standardized, Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR)-based application programming interfaces (APIs), and a common data foundation such as the United States Core Data for Interoperability Version-3 (USCDI v3). In parallel, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) initiatives have accelerated the transition to digital quality measures (dQMs), increasing the need for automated, multisource, standards-based data exchange aligned with real-time quality improvement. Using hypothetical use cases in vascular and behavioral neurology, we demonstrate how FHIR-based implementation guides could replace manual stroke quality reporting and enable the migration of cognitive assessment measures from legacy electronic clinical quality measures (eCQMs) to interoperable FHIR eCQMs, laying the groundwork for future dQMs. These examples highlight the potential of shared terminologies, structured neurologic observations, and API-enabled exchange, while underscoring persistent challenges, including limited availability of discrete neurologic data elements and the substantial effort required for mapping and governance. As the neurology ecosystem prepares for USCDI-aligned interoperability mandates taking effect in 2026, the neurology community plays a critical leadership role. Priorities include expanding neurologic data models and terminologies, ensuring that dQMs reflect clinical realities, strengthening governance across registries and networks, and enabling interoperable workflows that support remote monitoring and AI-enabled analytics. Together, these strategies position interoperability as a strategic imperative for the future of neurologic care, quality measurement, and research.

title: Standardising ocular surface photography for artificial intelligence: current limitations and a proposed roadmap.
text: Slit-lamp colour photography remains a cornerstone of anterior segment documentation and longitudinal monitoring. However, conventional slit-lamp photography has seen relatively limited technological advancement compared with the rapid development of quantitative anterior-segment modalities such as AS-OCT, Scheimpflug tomography and confocal microscopy. Despite the wide diffusion of digital cameras, smartphones, and high-end slit-lamp systems, ocular surface photography (OSP) remains hampered by the absence of standardised acquisition and processing protocols. The convex, aspheric geometry of the ocular surface, off-axis illumination, peripheral defocus, automatic colour correction, and pupil-driven exposure variation in retroillumination limit reproducibility, inter-device comparability, and clinical utility. In this review we critically appraise current OSP applications across major ocular surface conditions (dry eye disease, conjunctival hyperaemia, infectious keratitis, ocular surface burns, and ocular surface neoplasia), mapping the hardware, software, and reproducibility limitations that constrain clinical practice. We then examine how these limitations propagate into artificial intelligence (AI) development, where the absence of large, well-annotated, demographically diverse OSP datasets, together with the lack of reproducible quantitative phenotypes and reliable labels, is now the principal bottleneck to clinically deployable models; we discuss patient-level data partitioning and external validation, and outline how deep learning, federated learning and foundation models can both utilise and improve OSP. Finally, we propose a minimum acquisition and dataset specification, tiered by clinical setting from research to community screening, and a staged roadmap that combines hardware standardisation (focus-stacked, illumination-controlled, colour-calibrated acquisition), interoperable metadata-rich storage (DICOM where infrastructure permits), quantitative phenotype definition, and diverse international dataset collaborations, so that the ocular surface can benefit from quantitative imaging and AI as other areas of ophthalmology have begun to.

title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
text: We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome. We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model. The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR). Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

title: AI-Enhanced finite element analysis for optimal material selection in total knee replacement.
text: The increasing prevalence of total knee replacement (TKR) surgery and its association with aseptic loosening present a significant research challenge. This issue can be mitigated by selecting optimal materials for TKR components. This paper presents a hybrid approach combining Finite Element Method (FEM) with Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques for optimal material selection in TKR. Simulations of four normal movements-compression, distraction, medial bending, and lateral bending-were performed on a 3D model of the artificial knee. Four materials were evaluated: Cobalt-Chromium (Co-Cr), Zirconium (Zr), Stainless Steel, and Titanium (Ti). To simulate ligamentous constraints during distraction loading, a model of a nonlinear spring element was included, furnishing more physiologically realistic boundary conditions. An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) was trained on FEM simulation data to predict material performance with 98.7% accuracy for stress prediction (R2 = 0.987), while displacement prediction achieved R2 = 0.985. Multi-criteria decision-making using TOPSIS ranked Co-Cr as the optimal material under stress-prioritized weighting (0.6/0.4); though, sensitivity analysis revealed that Stainless Steel converts optimal when displacement/compliance is prioritized (0.4/0.6). Under axial compression of 1300 N, maximum stress for Co-Cr and Zr was 4.207 × 108N/m2 and 3.921 × 108N/m2, respectively. Under distraction: 4.321 × 108N/m2 and 4.142 × 108N/m2. Under medial bending: 1.101 × 108N/m2 and 1.088 × 108N/m2. Under lateral bending: 1.119 × 108N/m2 and 1.102 × 108N/m2. The AI-based approach reduced computational time by 73% compared to full FEM simulations while maintaining high prediction accuracy. This time-saving shows the promise of the surrogate model for large scale materials screening and patient specific implant optimization, but further biocompatibility and tribological validation will be required for clinical translation of these findings.

title: An interpretable machine learning model for predicting response to anti-GD2 combined with umbilical cord blood-derived natural killer cell immunotherapy in neuroblastoma.
text: Neuroblastoma remains a major therapeutic challenge for children with high-risk or relapsed/refractory disease. Anti-GD2 therapy combined with umbilical cord blood-derived natural killer (UCB-NK) cell therapy represents an emerging strategy, but responses vary substantially. Imaging and bone marrow assessments require specialized resources, creating a need for complementary tools based on routinely available data. However, whether serial routine peripheral blood measurements can support response prediction in this treatment setting remains unclear. Serial peripheral blood measurements from 42 patients were used to derive dynamic coupling features that reflected longitudinal trends and coordinated changes between biomarkers. These features were integrated with static variables to develop machine learning models for response prediction. Seven machine learning models were compared using the same repeated stratified cross-validation framework. Model selection considered discrimination, probability-estimation quality, and interpretability. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to interpret the final model. Considering cross-validated performance, the quality of probability estimates, and clinical interpretability, L2-regularized logistic regression was selected as the final model for response prediction. The model leveraged dynamic peripheral blood features to predict response to anti-GD2 combined with UCB-NK cell immunotherapy, achieving a cross-validated AUC of 0.873 (95% bootstrap CI, 0.735-0.976) and a Brier score of 0.131 (95% bootstrap CI, 0.087-0.182). SHAP analysis characterized the direction and magnitude of feature contributions to model predictions. This study developed an interpretable response-prediction model using serial routine peripheral blood tests obtained in clinical practice. The model may complement treatment-response assessment using routinely available data. However, validation in larger, independent cohorts is required before clinical use.

title: MicroRNAs in aflatoxin B1-associated hepatocellular carcinogenesis: a scoping review of molecular networks, multiomics evidence, machine learning and translational potentials.
text: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a foodborne hepatocarcinogen, but it remains unclear whether microRNA dysregulation reflects AFB1-associated hepatocarcinogenesis or general hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) biology. This scoping review mapped evidence linking AFB1 exposure, microRNA regulation, molecular mechanisms, multiomics, computational modelling, and machine learning approaches to HCC diagnostics, prognostics, and therapeutics. Peer-reviewed studies published from 2016 to 2026 were identified through Scopus, Embase, PubMed, and Web of Science, supplemented by citation searching, and screened using PRISMA ScR-aligned criteria. The final corpus comprised 104 unique studies classified by AFB1 attribution strength and evidence type across five strata spanning direct human AFB1 HCC microRNA evidence to general HCC contextual evidence. Experimental mechanistic studies predominated, whereas only one study directly combined measured AFB1 exposure, HCC, and microRNA assessment in humans. The study enrolled 366 HCC cases and 662 controls; circulating miR-4651 provided the strongest exposure-anchored clinical signal, discriminating AFB1-positive HCC with an area under the curve of 0.85, 78.1% sensitivity, and 92.1% specificity. Other studies evaluated exposure-responsive hepatotoxicity, experimental malignant transformation, or rat hepatocarcinogenesis, which cannot be considered interchangeable endpoints. Functionally investigated injury candidates included miR-1679 and miR-124a-3p. Multiomics findings implicated DNA damage, methylation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, inflammation, and metabolic dysregulation, although pathway overlap was heterogeneous and independent functional confirmation was limited. Computational and machine learning studies have expanded network and feature prioritisation, but they have often relied on inferred exposure and limited external validation. Direct human evidence remains scarce, and candidate microRNAs occupy different validation stages. Biological plausibility does not establish clinical readiness; multicentre exposure-anchored validation, harmonised assays and prospective evaluation are required.

title: Design and evaluation of probe-capture sequencing for clinical Neisseria gonorrhoeae specimens
text: Characterizing the molecular epidemiology of Neisseria gonorrhoeae is essential for understanding disease burden, elucidating transmission dynamics, and informing clinical decision-making and public health interventions. Given that routine, culture-independent diagnostics rapidly and sensitively detect this difficult-to-cultivate pathogen, aligning genomic surveillance with these workflows is necessary to understand its epidemiology and evolutionary dynamics. To address this challenge, we investigated the utility of probe-capture sequencing to selectively enrich for pathogen-specific DNA during next-generation sequencing. Custom biotinylated oligonucleotide baits were designed using genetic information from publicly available genomes hosted on Pathogenwatch. Of the 32,574 assemblies, 2,877 representative genomes were selected to inform probe generation using core genome amino acid distance clustering and representation of unique resistance-associated genotypes and predicted resistance phenotypes. The resulting probe set provided generous coverage of the reference genome, N. gonorrhoeae FA 1090, with 94.6% nucleotide coverage and 99.3% of annotated genes covered by at least one probe. Piloting this technology on 12 clinical urine specimens with variable relative pathogen abundances revealed that probe-capture sequencing substantially increased the relative abundance of N. gonorrhoeae sequence reads from a complex sample (fold-change range, 226 - 2046), enabling considerable genome coverage, the construction of high-quality genome assemblies, and the detection of resistance-associated genotypes. These findings demonstrate that probe-capture sequencing is a viable method for enriching N. gonorrhoeae genetic material from clinical samples, enabling culture-independent genomic investigations into the epidemiology of hard-to-culture pathogens and providing actionable insights to inform clinical and public health interventions. IMPORTANCEUnderstanding the molecular epidemiology of bacterial pathogens can illuminate population diversity, transmission dynamics, and genotypes associated with bacterial traits and clinical outcomes. Difficulties in cultivation hinder our ability to understand the epidemiology of Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Aligning genomic surveillance methodologies with existing clinical diagnostic modalities is essential to guiding the implementation of innovative genomic surveillance. In this paper, we used representative public genome assemblies to design custom biotinylated oligonucleotide baits to successfully increase pathogen-specific DNA yield from complex clinical urine specimens during next-generation sequencing. Probe-capture sequencing markedly improved detection of pathogen-specific genetic material from clinical specimens, enabling construction of high-quality genome assemblies and detection of resistance-associated genotypes. Collectively, we demonstrate that probe-capture sequencing is a viable method for sequencing hard-to-culture pathogens from clinical specimens, highlighting how this technology could strengthen genomic investigations into the epidemiology of these pathogens and provide actionable insights to inform clinical decision-making and public health interventions.

title: Anonymous in Name Only: A Critical Review and a Reidentification Exercise on the European Commission's Anonymization Measures for Google Search Data under Article 6(11) of the DMA
text: In July 2026, the European Commission (EC) set out the anonymization measures Alphabet must implement to share Google Search data with competing search engines under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act. As the first concrete illustration of how the EC operationalizes anonymization under the EU digital rulebook, this methodology could become a regulatory benchmark. In this paper, we show why it should not. We critically review the anonymization measures proposed by the EC, from the characterization of residual risk to the suppression thresholds and the reliance on contractual safeguards. For each of those issues, we highlight significant conceptual flaws, and, where applicable, we illustrate these flaws with empirical observations from real Google Search data provided by Alphabet and protected under the EC's measures. Importantly, we present examples of low-effort reidentification, record linkage, and confidential attribute inference achieved through straightforward and automatable attack patterns. Our findings show that the approach of the EC relies on unjustified heuristics rather than formal privacy guarantees, underestimates the risks inherent in free-text search queries, and sacrifices data utility without achieving meaningful protection. We also demonstrate that the proposed measures do not meet any of the three anonymization criteria established by the European Data Protection Board (EDPB): no record isolation, no linkage, and no inference. Practitioners and regulators are therefore cautioned against treating these measures as a sound anonymization practice.

title: Integrated manufacturing platform for cortical organoids reveals early phosphatase and prefoldin dysregulation in MAPT V337M neurons
text: Human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived cortical organoids are powerful models but are often limited by low efficiency, variability, and stress-related artifacts. To address these challenges, we developed a scalable organoid platform with end-to-end quality control (QC) metrics spanning manufacturing and single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq), developed using eight MAPT mutation isogenic line sets relevant to frontotemporal dementia (FTD-tau). Using a 96 slit-well format, we achieved ~100% organoid formation across 64 lines. Controlled-release FGF2 enhanced hPSC pluripotency and reduced mesendodermal contaminants, while optimized SB431542 dosing enhanced cortical patterning across lines with variable TGFBR1/ALK5 expression. The resulting organoids displayed transcriptomic profiles and low-stress signatures closely aligned with the developing human cortex. Applying a cortical organoid scRNA-seq index (CortiCOSI), we identified early dysregulation of phosphatase regulators ( PPP2CA, ANP32A ) and the prefoldin subunit PFDN6 in MAPT V337M excitatory neurons before tau hyperphosphorylation and oligomerization. This platform improves scalability, reproducibility, and mechanistic insight in cortical organoid studies.

title: Survey of the human proteostasis network: the ubiquitin-proteasome system
text: Modification by ubiquitination governs the half-lives of thousands of proteins that are fated for elimination by either the proteasome or autophagy pathways, depending on the intricate architectures of ubiquitin modification. This system mediates quality control for individual proteins, protein complexes, and organelles, as well as myriad purely regulatory functions. Here we provide a comprehensive survey of the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), the scope of which is at present poorly defined. title: Edición génica in vivo de PCSK9 en la prevención cardiovascular aterosclerótica: de la validación genética a la clínica
text: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is the primary causal and modifiable risk factor.Available lipid-lowering therapies-statins, ezetimibe, anti-PCSK9 monoclonal antibodies, and RNA interference-have been shown to reduce cardiovascular events, but they require long-term administration and are limited by efficacy, adherence, cost, and access.Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is, to date, the most genetically validated target for the development of in vivo gene-editing strategies aimed at achieving a permanent reduction in LDL-C through a single therapeutic administration.This review describes the biology of PCSK9, the available gene-editing platforms-CRISPR-Cas9, base editing, and primer editing-and their delivery to hepatocytes via lipid nanoparticles.It summarizes preclinical data and ongoing clinical trials (VERVE-101, VERVE-102, and YOLT-101) showing sustained, dose-dependent reductions in LDL-C following a single infusion, with acceptable short-term safety profiles.Finally, the long-term safety, regulatory, economic, and ethical challenges that will determine the eventual translation of this technology into routine clinical practice are discussed.

title: Integrated manufacturing platform for cortical organoids reveals early phosphatase and prefoldin dysregulation in MAPT V337M neurons
text: Human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived cortical organoids are powerful models but are often limited by low efficiency, variability, and stress-related artifacts. To address these challenges, we developed a scalable organoid platform with end-to-end quality control (QC) metrics spanning manufacturing and single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq), developed using eight MAPT mutation isogenic line sets relevant to frontotemporal dementia (FTD-tau). Using a 96 slit-well format, we achieved ~100% organoid formation across 64 lines. Controlled-release FGF2 enhanced hPSC pluripotency and reduced mesendodermal contaminants, while optimized SB431542 dosing enhanced cortical patterning across lines with variable TGFBR1/ALK5 expression. The resulting organoids displayed transcriptomic profiles and low-stress signatures closely aligned with the developing human cortex. Applying a cortical organoid scRNA-seq index (CortiCOSI), we identified early dysregulation of phosphatase regulators ( PPP2CA, ANP32A ) and the prefoldin subunit PFDN6 in MAPT V337M excitatory neurons before tau hyperphosphorylation and oligomerization. This platform improves scalability, reproducibility, and mechanistic insight in cortical organoid studies.

title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals organizational properties of the mouse spinal cord and alterations in neuropathic pain
text: The spinal cord integrates diverse somatosensory inputs and executes motor outputs through anatomically and functionally distinct circuits. Here, we employed spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomic profiling of the adult mouse spinal cord to gain insights into the organizational logic of the spinal cord. Our results reveal distinct spatial and laminar distributions of neuronal subtypes, including axial level and sex-specific differences. Many neuronal subtypes exhibit lamina-specific somatic proximities, suggesting potential regionally specific connectivity. Additionally, neuronal subtypes within the dorsal horn exhibit a wide range of predicted cell-cell communication motifs, as assessed by the spatial distribution of neuropeptide- and other ligand-receptor pairs. Finally, we identified several neuronal subtypes with altered transcriptomic states and predicted cell–cell communications in a model of neuropathic pain. This spatially resolved cellular and molecular map of the spinal cord will facilitate the decoding of circuit mechanisms underlying somatosensory and motor functions in health and disease.

title: Bioimaging and comparative genomics for characterization of surface-bacteria isolated from a blood bank facility
text: Blood banks represent highly controlled healthcare environments where microbiological surveillance has traditionally focused on Blood products rather than environmental microbial reservoirs. Despite their crucial role in transfusion safety, the ecology of surface-associated microorganisms remains poorly understood. This cross-sectional study characterized culturable bacteria recovered from Blood-bank surfaces. We combined scanning electron microscopy, culture-based microbiology, phenotypic characterization, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, and whole-genome sequencing to investigate whether surfaces within a public blood bank facility (BBF) constitute reservoirs of environmentally derived bacteria with putative traits potentially relevant to environmental survival. Samples collected from a public BBF in Tucumán, Argentina yielded 36 culturable bacterial isolates, predominantly Gram-positive taxa together with a limited number of opportunistic Gram-negative species. Several isolates showed reduced susceptibility to various groups of antimicrobials; furthermore, several strains exhibited strong biofilm formation, production of amyloid-like fibers, motility, and hemolytic activity. Whole-genome sequencing of six representative isolates supported previous species affiliations, identified genes related to antimicrobial resistance, adhesion, biofilm formation, stress adaptation, and cytotoxicity, highlighting the importance of integrating genomic and phenotypic analyses. Notably, BS-018 showed a low ANI to the reported comparison genome, but its taxonomic assignment remains unresolved. Blood bank surfaces function as localized environmental conditions favoring bacteria with potential persistence-associated traits. This study identified environmental bacterial isolates exhibiting phenotypic and genomic characteristics potentially relevant to biosafety surveillance. Our results support incorporating integrated bioimaging, phenotypic characterization, and environmental surveillance with genomic resolution into infection prevention strategies and transfusion biosafety programs.

title: Programmable and selective silencing of oncogenic fusion transcripts by CRISPR-Cas13b via breakpoint sequence recognition
text: Oncogenic gene fusions are key drivers of cancer, yet most remain undruggable by current therapies. title: TactiDex: A Real-World Tactile-Guided Benchmark for Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation
text: Tactile feedback is fundamental to Hand-Object Interaction (HOI), governing contact formation, force regulation, and stable manipulation, making it essential for achieving true human-like dexterous manipulation. Yet, current human-to-robot dexterous transfer pipelines primarily rely on kinematic trajectories, resulting in motion imitation without physically grounded interaction. To address this, we introduce TactiDex, a real-world tactile-guided benchmark specifically designed to move dexterous manipulation beyond kinematic mimicry toward contact-level human-likeness. TactiDex provides a comprehensive dataset that elegantly aligns whole-hand tactile signals with multi-granularity kinematic and object states, coupled with standardized evaluation metrics. Building upon this data paradigm, we propose a tactile-driven transfer framework that effectively translates human demonstrations into physically plausible robotic execution. We introduce TactiSkill, a framework built upon a novel tri-component tactile reward that innovatively uses tactile signals as structured supervision. This reward unifies guidance, human-like alignment, and contact constraints into a single objective. Through comprehensive experiments on both single and bimanual tasks, we demonstrate that TactiSkill achieves superior performance in manipulation success and physical realism. This work lays a crucial foundation for advancing tactile-aware dexterous manipulation. Our project page at https://tactidex.github.io/.

title: Multimodal single-cell epigenomic and 3D genome atlas of the human basal ganglia
text: Abstract The basal ganglia (BG) underlie motor control, reward processing, and many neurological and psychiatric disorders, but a comprehensive epigenomic and 3D-genome atlas of the human BG is lacking. Here we present a multimodal single-cell atlas profiling DNA methylation and 3D chromatin conformation in 261,331 nuclei (snm3C-seq) across eight subregions, resolving 12 classes, 31 subclasses, and 59 groups. Harmonized under the HMBA basal-ganglia consensus taxonomy, this atlas integrates with matched RNA, ATAC-seq, and histone-modification data across five regulatory layers. We identify millions of cell-type- and region-specific differentially methylated regions enriched for distinct transcription factor motifs and link them to disease-associated heritability. Neuron-specific loops dominate cell-type-specific 3D contact remodeling, while most non-neuron-specific loops are constitutive. Among spiny projection neurons (SPNs), chromatin loops, rather than TAD boundaries, distinguish D1, D2, and eccentric SPN subclasses, with eccentric SPNs showing the most loop-level reorganization among the three. We characterize STR D2 SMYD2-HTR7 SPN, a newly recognized POU6F2⁺ D2-SPN subtype, and reveal region-specific methylation and contact gradients of disease-associated genes, including CADM1 and PDE8B. Integrative gene-regulatory networks reconstruct cell-type-resolved enhancer-promoter links to interpret Parkinson’s disease risk variants at SNCA. Finally, MERFISH spatial profiling combined with cross-species Patch-seq identifies non-SPN neuronal subtypes, including a MOXD1⁺ striosomal STR FS PTHLH-PVALB GABA subtype with distinct electrophysiology, partitioning across the striatal matrix-striosome boundary. Neuron-specific loops dominate cell-type-specific 3D contact remodeling in the human BG, whereas most non-neuron-specific loops are constitutive. Chromatin loops are the primary distinguishing feature among D1, D2, and eccentric SPN subclasses, with eccentric SPNs being the most 3D-reorganized. Integrated regulatory maps link cell-type-specific enhancers to disease-associated genetic risk in the human basal ganglia. Non-SPN interneurons differ in distribution and in transcriptional and epigenetic identity across the matrix-striosome boundary.

title: The FMR1 isoform landscape reveals new spliced variants in women’s blood and ovarian tissues
text: Abstract FMR1 encodes fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMRP), an RNA-binding protein involved in post-transcriptional regulation and highly expressed in ovarian tissue. Although extensive alternative splicing of FMR1 has been described, the full-set transcript landscape in ovarian cells remains incompletely characterized. Here, we used Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read amplicon sequencing to characterize full-length FMR1 transcripts spanning exons 1–17 in human blood and ovarian granulosa cells. We identified 30 high-confidence isoforms accounting for 95% of amplicon-captured FMR1 expression. The predominant transcripts lacked exon 12 and retained exon 14, consistent with previous reports. Long-read sequencing also resolved previously uncharacterized splicing events, including infrequent splice-site usage in exons 15 and 17, exon 11 skipping, and partial retention of introns 2 and 7. Several transcripts preserve the open reading frame, whereas others introduce premature termination codons and may undergo nonsense-mediated decay or produce truncated FMRP isoforms. Notably, the FMR1 expression profile was conserved between blood and granulosa cells, indicating that blood may serve as an accessible proxy tissue for studying FMR1 isoform expression. These findings expand the known FMR1 transcript repertoire and demonstrate the value of long-read sequencing for resolving complex splicing, providing a basis for investigating these isoforms’ role in ovarian function.

title: NPlasmid-seq: Cas9-encoded terminal signatures enable molecule-level nanopore quality control of vector and IVT-template plasmids
text: Abstract Consensus-based plasmid quality control can overlook structural heterogeneity within a preparation. We developed NPlasmid-seq, a Cas9-guided nanopore workflow that encodes sample identity through paired terminal signatures generated at predefined backbone positions, without sample-specific oligonucleotide barcodes. We cleavage-validated 24 sgRNAs. In five representative assigned read bins, each bin showed its strongest sequence agreement with its cognate reference. Contaminant detection was evaluated with a single class-specific classifier applied both to computational read mixtures and to physical DNA mixtures, placing the two designs on a common scale. In computational read mixtures of 5,000 reads, a contaminant was detected in all 20 independent subsamples at each of 0.2%, 0.5%, 1% and 5% abundance and in 13 of 20 subsamples at 0.1%; precision was 1.000 in all 100 subsamples, with no false-positive calls among 493,200 reads from the declared target plasmid. In physical DNA mixtures carried through cleavage, pooled library preparation and sequencing, a contaminant was detected in all six samples prepared at 0.5 mol% input and all six at 1 mol%. Observed read fractions did not distinguish the 0.5 and 1 mol% input levels. Instead, they differed systematically by 4.0-fold between preparation pools, a larger effect than the difference between the two input levels. We therefore interpret the workflow as a detector, not a quantifier, of sub-percent contamination. Read-level analysis identified a recurrent 93-bp deletion in 61.7% of reads from a preparation that had passed consensus-based quality control. Sanger genotyping of 24 colonies identified deletion-type profiles in 10 colonies and intact-type profiles in three. The remaining 11 colonies showed double peaks at the diagnostic locus, consistent with coexistence of both sequence forms within individual clones. In in vitro transcription template plasmids, longer poly(A) tracts were associated with higher multimeric-read fractions. Across ten matched A90 culture pairs, propagation at 30 °C reduced these fractions relative to 37 °C (paired t-test, P = 0.0098). These measurements describe recovered read populations, not absolute molecular abundances. NPlasmid-seq therefore complements consensus validation by revealing sequence and structural heterogeneity within a preparation and by identifying a culture condition associated with a lower multimeric-read fraction.

title: ExPert infers causal perturbations from cell states across biological and clinical contexts
text: ABSTRACT Pooled single-cell CRISPR screens have driven substantial effort toward models predicting the response to a perturbation. We posed the inverse question: which perturbation produced an observed cell state? Here we developed ExPert (Extracting Perturbations), which learns one prototype per perturbation in a latent space shared by 12 cellular contexts, trained on 8,964 perturbations and 19.5 million cells, and ranks 19,895 candidate genes per query, over half absent from training. ExPert more than doubled held-out-context recall over the best existing method with 1,000-fold less compute, and transferred without retraining to drugs, protein degradation and combinations. In alcohol-associated liver disease it implicated mRNA export, unchanged in expression, and we experimentally confirmed nuclear poly(A) retention and isoform switching. In primary mitochondrial disease it recovered the affected complex from blood, localized the signal to monocytes, and flagged a misdiagnosed control. Perturbation atlases can thus be queried in reverse, from state to likely driver.

title: Multi-dataset INST 13C metabolic flux analysis reveals robust fluxes but variable metabolite pools
text: Isotopically non-stationary metabolic flux analysis (INST 13 C-MFA) provides unique insights into cellular physiology but remains limited by low throughput and high experimental costs. This is particularly relevant for emerging C1/C2 bioprocesses, where isotopically stationary 13 C-MFA is generally uninformative due to limited labeling diversity. We developed a miniaturized and automated workflow that combines parallelized transient isotope labeling experiments with high-performance computational analysis to enable INST 13 C-MFA at microliter scale. Applied to an evolved Corynebacterium glutamicum strain growing on ethanol, robotic micro-cultivations with complementary tracers, hot isopropanol quenching, and LC-QToF-MS analytics yielded highly informative datasets. Joint analysis produced the first quantitative flux map of ethanol metabolism in evolved C. glutamicum , revealing strong glyoxylate shunt activity. Multi-dataset INST 13 C-MFA further showed that integrating complementary ILEs increased net flux resolution and preserved flux estimates across tracers and independent experimental runs, while pool size estimates remained dataset-specific. Together, this work establishes a cost-efficient, scalable framework for quantitative fluxomics and its integration into biofoundry pipelines, enabling systematic physiological characterization of microorganisms growing on sustainable C1/C2 feedstocks.

title: Generating interesting scientific ideas using knowledge graphs and LLMs: Evaluations with 100 research group leaders
text: The rapid growth of scientific literature makes it increasingly challenging for researchers to identify novel and impactful ideas, especially across disciplines. Modern AI systems offer new opportunities for scientific ideation, but how compelling are AI-generated ideas, and how can their quality be improved? Here, we introduce SCIMUSE , which generates personalized research ideas using a knowledge graph of 58 million papers and a large language model (LLM). A central focus of this work is to understand how interesting these ideas are. Therefore, we conducted a large-scale evaluation in which more than 100 research group leaders—spanning the natural sciences to the humanities—rated over 4,400 personalized ideas according to their level of interest. Overall, expert ratings were modest (mean 2.40 on a 5-point scale, most common rating 1), while 24.9% of ideas were rated 4 or 5. We find that supplying concept pairs selected using the knowledge graph does not improve expert-rated interest over a titles-only GPT baseline. High-citation-predicted pairs even showed a weak tendency (1.94 σ ) toward lower interest than random pairs. Nevertheless, graph features can be used to control properties of ideas, and, using this unique evaluation dataset, we show that idea interest can be predicted with both a supervised neural network based on graph features and a zero-shot ranking approach based on an LLM. Our work provides an AI methodology for generating scientific ideas and a large-scale interdisciplinary expert evaluation, paving the way to study and improve difficult-to-measure metrics such as expert-perceived scientific interestingness.

title: BEYOND RECOMMENDATIONS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF VALUES, OUTCOMES AND IMPACT OF HEALTH TECHNOLOGY ASSESSMENT AGENCIES WORLDWIDE
text: IntroductionHealth Technology Assessment (HTA) agencies are increasingly required to demonstrate their added value for health systems, yet evidence on their real-world performance remains limited and heterogeneous.This systematic review aimed to describe the characteristics, perceived value, outcomes and impact of governmental HTA bodies worldwide. MethodsWe searched biomedical databases, registries, grey literature and websites of HTA agencies and international networks, without language or date restrictions, following Cochrane and PRISMA guidance.Eligible documents reported empirical data or structured opinions on governmental HTA agencies whose role is defined in law or equivalent regulation and/or whose recommendations are binding or otherwise mandatory for at least one health subsystem; purely theoretical pieces and non-governmental initiatives were excluded.A qualitative narrative and thematic synthesis was undertaken. ResultsWe identified 56 governmental HTA agencies, 43 established by law, operating across diverse regions and health-system arrangements.Stakeholders consistently valued these agencies for credibility, scientific rigor and their contribution to transparent, equity-oriented priority setting.Quantitative evidence showed wide variation in HTA report production, economic effects and influence on technology adoption, clinical practice and budgetary outcomes, with some agencies generating substantial savings and shaping coverage and disinvestment decisions.Impact was often indirect, context-dependent, more frequently documented at policy than clinical level.Long-term and equity-focused outcomes were sparsely reported.
